docs.title: datarecord
docs.text:
A record holds labeled data with a declared schema. Its labels sit on axes called dims. A multi-dim is a dim whose labels are tuples of other dims' labels, listing which combinations exist. Properties describe single labels, and attributes hold values at coordinates. The schema declares what may exist, and the data says what does.

A record can be one parquet directory or a tree of layers, and a reader reads both through one interface. A layer adds a partial record on top of its parent, so a scenario variant stores only the rows it changes. Any parquet reader can open a record's directory.

datarecord depends on duckdb, pydantic and mathspec, and names no modelling framework. A framework consumes a record, a workflow engine produces one, and neither needs to know how the other works.

pip install datarecord           # core
pip install datarecord[pypsa]    # with the PyPSA tool

The package does not yet declare mathspec, which is not on PyPI. Install it alongside from GitHub, at the commit pixi.toml pins (installation).

from datarecord import Workspace

ws = Workspace()
record = ws.at("s3://bucket/my-record/")

record.properties["entity"].df()  # one row per entity, its properties
record.attributes["p_max_pu"].df()  # long value rows
record.flags(ctype="Generator")  # which axes each attribute uses

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text: All notable changes to datarecord are documented here. The format follows Keep a Changelog.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Properties. The schema has a properties section (PropertySpec) that declares, per dim or multi-dim, the values that describe one label. A record stores them as columns of dims/<dim>.parquet. A caller names a property as subject.name, as in set("bus.x", ...) and default_by keys such as {"entity.ctype": {...}}. Schema.resolve(name) returns the spec of a name, and Schema.column_type takes the property's subject. A property may share its name with an attribute, a dim or a property of another subject.
  • A property declares exactly one of dtype and one_of: <dim>. A property with one_of refers to that dim, and its values are live labels of that dim. set and add check them, and the writer checks every layer. remove(dim, labels) fails while such a property still holds a label.
  • A property that refers to a dim with one_of, on a subject in partial, categorizes the subject. Categories select labels in flags(ctype="Generator") and in set("p_max_pu", 0.9, ctype="Generator"). default_by gives a default per category. Schema.categorizing lists the categorizing properties of a subject.
  • A dim of dtype str may declare one_of: [...], as in mathspec. Its column is an ENUM of those labels, add refuses a label outside the list, and its axis holds the labels that were added.
  • WorkingRecord edits any dim: add(dim, labels, **properties), remove(dim, labels) and set(name, value, **coords). set writes attributes and properties, and a property keyword selects labels when set is called.
  • A multi-dim is a broadcast coordinate like any dim. A NULL multi-dim value means every tuple of the multi-dim, and partial may name a multi-dim.
  • Workspace holds the DuckDB database and Store holds one location. A store keeps a revision file per revision as revisions/<id>.json, so a Revision serialises as its location and id and reads its ancestry in a new process. ws.con is the cursor of the calling thread. The write and edit boundary rejects a relation from another connection or thread.
  • Writing is store.root(source), rev.child(source) and ws.write(source, uri). rev.child(w.edits) writes the edits of a WorkingRecord as a child layer, and ws.write(w, uri) writes the flattened record. A tree write puts the revision file last, so a failed write leaves no revision and does not widen the manifest.
  • A store or standalone directory on s3://, through boto3 behind the datarecord[remote] extra and configured by the AWS environment. Revision files are written create-only and the manifest by compare-and-swap, so two writers that widen one schema both keep their widening.
  • Tool.to_datarecord(model, con) takes the connection that its frames are planned on.
  • Removing an entity removes the group tuples that name it, and the values of a tuple go with it. An add of the name revives the entity alone. A layer that adds a tuple naming a removed label, or removes a label that a tuple names, fails at write.
  • A layer that changes an axis or a group restates it whole, in order. A label is removed where a restatement omits a label that the previous one held, and its order is the file's row order. The deepest file for an axis or group is the answer for a node. A WorkingRecord stages an edited axis or group whole, copied from the base at its first edit. A materialised node holds copies of the deepest files in resolved/dims/ and resolved/groups/.
  • WorkingRecord.set checks that an attribute value names a label that its dim's axis, as staged, holds, for every dim, and a tuple that its group, as staged, holds. add checks that each label of a tuple is on its axis as staged, and that a value of a property with one_of is a label of that dim as staged. write_layer checks every attribute row against the final axes and groups of the layer, and every group tuple against the final axes. Each check is one DuckDB anti-join.
  • A schema is checked at load. A dim, group, group coordinate or attribute name that holds " or ., starts with _, is a column that datarecord writes itself (value, layer_uuid and others, ignoring case), or differs from another name only in case fails with an error that names each offender. Based on #26 by @FBumann.
  • A manifest with an unknown key fails to load with pydantic's ValidationError.
  • The PyPSA tool declares buses and carriers as dims. A bus is a label of bus and a carrier a label of carrier. The properties of bus are carrier, type, x, y, unit and location, and those of carrier are color and nice_name. v_nom, v_mag_pu_*, co2_emissions, max_growth, max_relative_growth and custom bus or carrier columns are attributes over their dim. marginal_price, v_mag_pu and v_ang are results over bus, and build sets them back. to_datarecord adds every carrier that a component names and carrier does not list, and stores "" as NULL. verify reports an entity attached to no bus.
  • The PyPSA tool declares the dims ctype and role with one_of, and entity.ctype, entity.carrier and connection.role as properties. partial is {"entity", "bus", "scenario", "connection"}.
  • PyPSA SubNetworks are labels of the dim sub_network, without a suffix. sub_network.carrier refers to carrier, and slack_bus is a property over sub_network. A solve that has SubNetworks restates the sub_network axis, and a solve without them restates it empty where the record has SubNetworks.
  • The PyPSA tool stores per-port results on connections like per-port inputs. p0, p1, p2 and a one-port type's p are one result p over the connection group, with a row per (entity, bus) that keeps the port's sign. q works the same way. Link.p and Process.p are p_internal, and a three-port Link's p2 is a declared result.
  • The PyPSA tool stores a Process's rate0, rate1, rate2 as one input rate over connection, static or per snapshot, and build puts each row back in its port's column. rate declares no default, so its ports default to -1 and 1.
  • The PyPSA tool round-trips multi-period networks. snapshot is one flat dim next to period, and each snapshot has a property snapshot.period with one_of: period, so period=2030 selects the snapshots of one period. A snapshot is labelled by its timestep where no timestep repeats across periods, and by its position otherwise, with the timestep in snapshot.timestep. build restores snapshots, investment periods, time series and both weightings.
  • The PyPSA tool round-trips snapshot and period weightings: snapshot_weighting_objective, _stores and _generators over snapshot, period_weighting_objective and _years over period, and scenario_weight.
  • The PyPSA tool round-trips a network's shapes. A geometry is stored as WKT in attributes/geometry.parquet, the CRS is crs in the schema's meta, and build restores n.shapes as a GeoDataFrame in that CRS.
  • PyPSA.to_datarecord(n, con, results_only=True, base=record) writes a solve as a thin layer. The layer restates the SubNetworks of base and sets NULL on the results of base that it does not write again. A NULL series value on export leaves the component at its static value.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Groups are multi-dims. A dim declared under dimensions with over, and neither dtype nor one_of, is a multi-dim: its labels are tuples of other dims' labels, carried as one struct column named for it. Its table is dims/<multi-dim>.parquet, keyed by that column with its properties beside it; groups/ and resolved/groups/ are gone, so every record with a group is written again. record.dims["connection"] is the struct column alone and record.properties["connection"] adds role. add and remove take a multi-dim's tuples as a frame holding its struct column, so add("connection", record.dims["connection"]) round-trips, or one with a column per coordinate instead, or as a list of mappings from coordinate to label. connection.bus names a coordinate wherever subject.name stands, and set refuses it. A multi-dim is never categorized, and no property refers to one. New on Schema: multi_dims, over, multi_dims_of, check_multi_dim_columns and coordinate_over; dims lists every dim but the multi-dims. The PyPSA tool declares connection under dimensions.
  • The design pages are grouped by topic: the data model, layers, using a record, storage, frameworks and the package. Each old design page URL redirects to its new page. The usage pages are organised by task, and the API reference uses the design section names.
  • An attribute over a multi-dim carries it as one struct column named for it, with a field per coordinate, such as connection STRUCT(entity, bus). Its table is keyed by that column, and dims/connection.parquet is connection STRUCT(entity, bus) | role. The PyPSA tool declares no bus attribute. A port's bus is the connection tuple.
  • The dims that a multi-dim draws on broadcast. A per-bus value with bus = NULL holds for every bus, and bus must be in partial to patch one bus at a time. WorkingRecord.set still takes bus=. Naming a multi-dim next to a dim that one of its coordinates is named for, as in dims={"connection", "bus"}, is an error.
  • entity is an ordinary dim. It broadcasts, and it must be in partial to be patched or categorized per label. entity_type is entity.ctype.
  • An attribute reaches every label that its dims address, whatever the categories of the labels. A NULL on a categorized dim reaches every label. flags(**categories) holds every attribute with a row that reaches a matching label. The PyPSA tool keeps the per-type vocabulary. build leaves out a value that its type does not take and reports it in Requirements.ignored, and to_datarecord records custom entity columns per type in the schema's meta.
  • Every layer holds its attributes in one attributes/ directory, and a result inherits through layers like any attribute. The PyPSA tool declares its outputs as attributes, and build copies them.
  • record.dims, properties and attributes return DuckDBPyRelations. Frames and LazyFrames are now Relations and LazyRelations. set, add and the writer take a relation or a pandas, polars or arrow frame, which DuckDB reads with its own scanner. They refuse timestamps with a time zone and cast a column only to a wider type of its kind. A dtype is mathspec's: float, int, bool, str or datetime.
  • The owner map's key is the partial dims and groups plus attribute. A dim or group outside partial is owned whole, so a layer that patches one connection's value restates every connection's. The PyPSA tool declares partial so that it keeps per-connection ownership. Schema.input_key is Schema.owner_map_key, Schema.input_columns is Schema.owner_map_columns, and Requirements.unsupported_keys reports "owner_map_key".
  • A Record is constructed from revision_id, sources, workspace and schema. A caller reads it through its mappings: rev.record.sources, dims[dim], properties[dim] and attributes[name]. attributes[name] raises KeyError for an undeclared attribute.
  • PyPSA.build raises TypeError for a RecordLike that is not a Record. Schema.long_columns_for raises KeyError for an attribute that the schema does not declare.
  • LayerData declares no frozen, and its axes(), groups() and attributes() return set[str]. A whole Record reaches the writer through the adapter for a RecordLike.
  • The modules live in the subpackages datarecord.schema, datarecord.resolve and datarecord.store. datarecord.record is datarecord.protocols, datarecord.files is datarecord.store.files, and datarecord.layered.categories is datarecord.schema.categories. The dtype helpers moved from datarecord.duck to datarecord.schema.dtypes. Every public name imports from datarecord.
  • A WorkingRecord folds its staged layer onto the folded axes, groups and removed labels of its base, which the workspace keeps as tables. Folding the staged edits opens no file of the base.
  • A label or group tuple that one layer removes and a later layer adds again takes its place where it is added again, in a working record, a written record and a materialised node.
  • A key held twice in a dims/ or groups/ file, and a column that is neither the key nor a declared property of its subject, fail at read. write_layer refuses a restatement that orders the labels of its parent differently.
  • A reference to a removed label in a group tuple or a property is checked in every subject that a layer restates, whole. A reference that an ancestor left dangling fails the next layer that restates its subject.
  • A standalone record's id is Schema.id, an optional field that its manifest.json carries. A tree's manifest carries none.
  • A value over a dim or group outside partial that names a removed label is dropped at read, including the per-bus values of a removed bus label. A materialised node keeps the removed labels in resolved/dead/.
  • attributes[name] returns the owned rows as written. A NULL coordinate stays NULL, rows of two layers may cover one coordinate, and the row order is unspecified. A consumer settles each coordinate by the broadcast rule, the row naming every dim the others there name winning. The owner map holds each layer's keys as written, plus one row naming both wherever a deeper layer's row crosses a parent's, so it grows with the rows layers write rather than with the labels a broadcast reaches.
  • A deeper layer owns only the coordinates its rows reach. A shallower row keeps every coordinate that no more specific row covers.
  • A label removed and added again takes every broadcast covering it, written before or after the removal, and no row that named it below the removal.
  • flags() counts a broadcast that more specific rows shadow at every label, and reports in varies and broadcast only the dims an attribute uses.
  • WorkingRecord.set writes a row that leaves a dim outside partial NULL out along the labels a parent row names there. The fold refuses a layer written otherwise that leaves such a crossing, naming the layer, the attribute, the dim and the key.
  • The writer accepts two rows that each name a dim the other leaves NULL where a row naming both is there, so ws.write(w, uri) writes a record of several layers. The read of a WorkingRecord refuses two staged rows that cross with no staged row naming both.
  • A materialised owner map keyed on another partial set than the schema's is ignored, and the read folds that node from its layers.
  • Attr.resolve and Schema.resolve take labels and flags, and settle each source by the broadcast rule over labels before a rename or a computation. settle(rel, labels, flags), exported from datarecord, does the same for one relation, dropping rows that name a label outside labels.

docs.title: Removed
docs.text:
• Group, the schema's groups section, Schema.groups, Schema.group_columns, Schema.group_type, Schema.groups_of, Schema.group_key, Schema.check_group_columns, Schema.field_over, RecordLike.groups, LayerData.groups() and LayerData.group(), WorkingRecord.add_group and WorkingRecord.remove_group.
  • set takes no expression. Compute the new values from attributes[name] and set the frame.
  • Dimension.within is gone. Every axis is keyed by its label alone, with labels unique across the dim. A nested dim is a property with one_of on the parent dim, such as snapshot.period with one_of: period. add takes no parent keys, and Schema.axis_key is gone.
  • Traits are gone: Trait, Schema.traits, Schema.attributes_for and Schema.properties_for.
  • Schema.results, Record.outputs, Kind, set(..., kind=...) and Tool.results are gone.
  • narwhals is not a dependency. Frames and LazyFrames are replaced as listed under Changed.
  • Resolver and Revision.resolver are gone, with with_source, inputs and the enumerators axes(), groups() and attributes() of the resolver.
  • write_record, Revision.create, the source-less Revision.child(), NewChild, Directory, commit, connect, layer_dir, DATARECORD_BASE_URI, the process default connection and on_connection are gone. Record.at takes a workspace.
  • Schema.membership_keys, Schema.group_coordinates, Group.coordinates, WorkingRecord.set's indexed_by, entity_types and the entity_type dim with its member files are gone.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• A pointwise set leaving one of two dims outside partial NULL keeps the rest of the series.
  • A broadcast reaches every label the record holds, including one added below a materialised revision or staged in a WorkingRecord, so materialising changes no answer.
  • set refuses a frame column that the schema does not declare for the attribute, and names the column and the columns it takes.
  • A later set replaces the rows of an earlier one that it covers. A row is covered where, at each coordinate, it names the same label or leaves NULL, including labels that a property keyword or a group's fields select. set("p_nom", 0.9, entity=["a"]) and then set("p_nom", 0.95) reads 0.95 at a. The other order keeps both rows, and a reads 0.9.
  • Within one layer the more specific row wins, so a layer that holds a default and its exception, such as set("p_nom", 0.95) and then set("p_nom", 0.9, entity=["a"]), reads one value at each coordinate. A row that names a label of a dim is more specific than a row that leaves that dim NULL. Two rows that cover one coordinate, where each names a dim that the other leaves NULL, fail at write and at read, naming the attribute and the coordinate.
  • A layer with two rows of one attribute that name the same labels at one breakpoint fails at write and at read, naming the attribute and the coordinate.
  • The writer casts every column to its declared dtype, as set does. An attribute's value is stored as its dtype, and an integer column under a float attribute is DOUBLE. A column of a type that does not fit its dtype, such as a string for a datetime dim or a float property, fails with the attribute, property or dim and its dtype named. A column that holds only NULLs passes as the NULL of its declared type, in set and add as well. The PyPSA tool's static rows keep an integer snapshot.
  • A label of a type that does not fit its dim's dtype fails with the dim and its dtype named. This covers a series index, mapping keys, a keyword of set, a multi-dim's coordinate keyword, the labels of add and remove, and a value of a property that refers to a dim. snapshot="2030-01-01" on a datetime dim is refused.
  • add checks that a property value is a label of its dim, and its error says to use one of the labels where the dim has one_of.
  • Removing an entity drops the values of every group row that names it, in any field. A contract over (from, to) loses its values when either party is removed, and flags(ctype) counts such a row for the type of each party.
  • Writing a layer whose manifest.json write keeps losing, as it does with a credential that can write the manifest but not read it, stops after ten attempts with an error that names s3:GetObject.
  • materialise() writes owner_map/inputs.parquet last and each file through a temporary name, so a node reads as materialised only when its cache is complete.
  • A fold cached before the manifest widened reads under the wider schema.
  • Reading an attribute over a partial dim scales linearly with the length of that dim. Folding the owner map no longer compares every row with every label of the dim's axis, so the first read of a record with long series is linear.
  • A record whose layers are all written scans its owner map once for the layers that own each attribute.
  • A pickled Revision unpickles through Workspace.process() and reads its ancestry, and pickles after .record was read.
  • A standalone record's manifest.json carries an id that ws.write mints, and the workspace keys its folds by that id. A record deleted and written again at one URI, or one relative path read from another working directory, reads its own folds. ws.at resolves a local path as ws.store does and refuses a manifest without an id.
  • ws.write to an existing empty directory raises FileExistsError up front and says that a standalone record is written to a URI that does not exist yet.
  • PyPSA.to_datarecord melts a time series whose component name holds a " or is snapshot or period, and accepts components whose names differ only by case, such as Gen and gen. PyPSA.build keeps the time series of a component named snapshot, or period in a multi-period network. No name is pasted into the UNPIVOT or PIVOT as an SQL identifier.
  • PyPSA.build turns a per-connection input back into PyPSA's port columns. efficiency on a Link's bus2 connection is efficiency2, static or per snapshot.
  • The PyPSA tool skips Line.v_nom and ShuntImpedance.v_nom, which PyPSA derives from the bus, and writes no Bus.p, q, control, generator or sub_network, so a solved network exports.

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text:
Contribution rules and conventions for datarecord. We welcome all contributors — a good place to start is the issues tagged "help wanted" and "good first issue".

By opening a pull request you represent that your contribution is your own original work and that you agree to license it under the project's MIT license.

docs.title: Reporting issues
docs.text:
Open a GitHub issue to report a bug or request a feature:

  • Report a bug — include a full traceback where there is one.
  • Request a feature.
  • Report a documentation problem.
  • Anything else.

docs.title: Development workflow
docs.text:
• Manage the environment with pixi and run every command inside it: pixi run <command> (e.g. pixi run pytest).
  • Run the test suite with pixi run test, and lint, format and type-check with pixi run lint before every commit — it runs the full lefthook hook set (ruff, prettier, taplo, typos, zizmor, reuse and mypy).
  • Lockfiles must stay consistent with package metadata: after any change to pixi.toml, run pixi lock.
  • The per-python environments (py311 … py314) mirror CI.

docs.title: Project conventions
docs.text:
• Branch off main for every change and open pull requests via the GitHub CLI (gh). A one-line commit message is fine for a small change; a larger one gets a summary line of at most 50 characters, a blank line, then a body describing what changed and why. Before opening a pull request, check you have updated CHANGELOG.md, added or updated documentation, and added tests for new functionality; give the pull request a clear summary of the change.
  • Write tests for new features and bug fixes under tests/ as test_*.py, reusing the shared fixtures in tests/fixtures.py and tests/conftest.py where useful. Run the tests after making changes and make sure they pass.
  • The design pages are the authoritative design. Cite them from a docstring's numpydoc Notes section rather than restating the argument — a comment that re-argues the design is a defect. When behaviour changes, update the page, not just the code. (Notes, not References: numpydoc discourages web links under References and expects entries there to augment a docstring rather than be required to understand it, which these are.)
  • Documentation is mkdocs: pixi run -e docs docs serves it locally, and pixi run -e docs docs-build is the strict build CI runs, which fails on a broken cross-reference. Every pull request publishes a rendered preview to https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/pr-<N>/, linked from a comment on the pull request itself; it is removed when the pull request closes, and a weekly job sweeps any that outlive it. Both live in .github/workflows/docs.yml.
  • No tool import may leak into core datarecord (module layout): everything framework-specific lives under datarecord/tools/ behind an optional extra.

docs.title: Design enhancement proposals
docs.text:
A change to the design starts as a design enhancement proposal (DEP): the argument for it, the design it lands, and usage examples.

  • Start from the template: copy it to docs/design/proposals/dep-NNNN-slug.md, where NNNN is the next free four-digit number, and append it to the end of the Enhancement proposals nav in mkdocs.yml. A number is never reused or reassigned.
  • Its header carries Status — Draft, Accepted, On hold, Implemented or Superseded, with the date — and Version, the release it ships in: Unreleased until the release that sets it.
  • Implementing it moves the design into the design pages and the usage examples into the usage pages, with as much of the argument as they need to stand on their own, and what it leaves open into open questions. The DEP stays as the record of the argument, and is not revised after: a change is a new DEP that replaces it.
  • Nothing outside the DEPs links to one — not a design or usage page, a docstring, a test or an error message — except open questions and the template. A DEP that is not yet implemented is not the design, and one that is has been superseded by the pages it landed in. pixi run lint fails on such a link.

docs.title: Architecture in one paragraph
docs.text: datarecord stores dimensioned attribute data with a declared schema: entities (named members of a type, unique record-wide), groups of them — a connection over (entity, bus) being the one every network has — attribute values over both, and the axes those values vary along. A record is defined by the RecordLike protocol — what it answers, not how it is stored — and a parquet directory is its on-disk form. The concrete Record folds a tree of layers resolved last-writer-wins, degenerating to a scan over a single directory (Record.at(uri)), so a consumer cannot tell how many layers it holds. Queries are DuckDB relations, staying lazy until fetched, and dtypes are mathspec's. Beyond duckdb, pydantic and mathspec, core depends on nothing. Keep new features consistent with this schema-declared, DuckDB-backed, lazily-evaluated design.

docs.title: Releasing
docs.text:
The version lives in [project].version in pyproject.toml; there is no VCS-derived versioning. CHANGELOG.md tracks user-facing changes under an [Unreleased] heading between releases.

To cut vX.Y.Z:

  1. Confirm pixi run test and pixi run -e docs docs-build pass — best done on a release pull request.
  2. Rename the [Unreleased] heading in CHANGELOG.md to vX.Y.Z with the release date, set version in pyproject.toml, and set Version to vX.Y.Z in every DEP header reading Unreleased.
  3. Merge the release pull request, then tag the merge commit vX.Y.Z and create the GitHub release from that tag.
  4. Open a follow-up adding a fresh [Unreleased] heading to CHANGELOG.md.

docs.title: AI-assisted contributions
docs.text: If you use AI tools when contributing, please read AGENTS.md for how AI-generated content must be marked and what we expect you to write by hand.

docs.title: Installing a user environment
docs.text:
Hint

If it is your first time using Python, we recommend pixi, conda, or uv as easy-to-use package managers. They are available for Windows, macOS, and GNU/Linux. It is always helpful to use dedicated environments.

You can install datarecord via all common package managers:

pixiuvcondapip 
pixi add --pypi datarecord

uv add datarecord

conda create -n datarecord "python>=3.12" "pip"
conda activate datarecord
pip install datarecord

pip install datarecord

datarecord is written and tested to be compatible with Python 3.12 and above. We recommend to use the latest version with active support (see endoflife.date).

docs.title: Installing a development environment
docs.text:
The install instructions are slightly different to create a development environment compared to a user environment:

git clone https://github.com/energy-models/datarecord
cd datarecord

pixi run test    # the test suite
pixi run lint    # ruff, prettier, taplo, typos, zizmor, reuse, mypy

For more detailed instructions specific to developing the datarecord codebase, see the contributing guide.

docs.title: API Reference
docs.text:
Generated from the docstrings. The docstrings cite the Design pages by link rather than restating the argument, so a symbol's "why" is one hop away; Usage is the worked prose.

Everything below is importable from the top-level package:

    AttributeSpec,
    Dimension,
    Flags,
    LazyRelations,
    Record,

docs.title: WorkingRecord
docs.text:
WorkingRecord(base: RecordLike)

Bases: Record

A Record whose last source is a staging area, plus the edit surface.

A Record in the type as well as in the fold: what it reads is the data with its pending edits applied, and it reads it by being one layer deeper than its base rather than by overlaying anything of its own. Every read member is inherited unchanged, so an edit reads back through the same code path a committed layer would.

Staged rows live in connection-scoped DuckDB tables, the only place a staged row exists: the reads fold them rather than holding a copy, so what is staged is asked of the reads themselves.

The source list is fixed at construction and never changes; a set changes what the last source's tables hold, not which sources there are. That is what lets the inherited members stay correct - they cache a key set only where the fold is stable, which a staged source makes it not.

Notes
  • WorkingRecord
  • staging
  • reading with pending edits

Stage edits over base, which must be a Record.

Raises:

Type Description TypeError

def __init__(self, base: RecordLike) -> None:
    """Stage edits over `base`, which must be a `Record`.

    Raises
    ------
    TypeError
        For any other `RecordLike`. A framework object hands over relations
        and has no layer layout behind it, so synthesising one would be
        rebuilding the format from a protocol that deliberately lacks it.
    """
    if not isinstance(base, Record):
        msg = (
            f"a `WorkingRecord` reads by folding its staged rows over the base's, "
            f"and a {type(base).__name__} has no layer layout to fold - pass a "
            f"`Record`, which `Revision.record` and `Workspace.at(uri)` both give"
        )
        raise TypeError(msg)
    # `object.__setattr__` throughout: the base is a frozen dataclass, and
    # these are set before `super().__init__` because the `StagedSource`
    # below reads them off `self`.
    object.__setattr__(self, "_layer_id", uuid4())
    object.__setattr__(self, "_staged", {})
    object.__setattr__(self, "_base", base)
    super().__init__(
        base.revision_id,
        [*base.sources, StagedSource(self, self._layer_id)],
        base.workspace,
        base.schema,
    )

def set(
    self,
    attribute: str,
    value: Any,
    **coords: Any,
) -> None:
    """Stage values of one attribute.

    Every coordinate is a keyword - `entity=`, `snapshot=`, a multi-dim's
    coordinate such as `bus=` or a corridor's `from=` - since which exist is declared
    rather than fixed. A keyword holds one label, fixing that coordinate, or
    a list of labels the value is staged at each of. A coordinate no keyword
    names is NULL, which by the broadcast rule is every label of it. The
    call replaces every row of `attribute` staged earlier that its own
    rows cover.

    `value` takes five forms:

    - a scalar, staged at every combination of the listed labels;
    - a sequence, aligned positionally to the one list keyword;
    - a mapping or a one-dimensional labelled series, keyed by labels of
      the series' `index.name` where that names a coordinate, else of the
      one coordinate no keyword names;
    - a long frame supplying its own keys, which keywords may complete with
      single labels.

    An attribute's values are long rows, whatever its `dims`. A property -
    a category included - patches one column of existing axis rows: a
    mapping or series from label to value, a `dim=` keyword naming the
    labels, or a scalar for every label the axis has. A multi-dim's
    property takes a scalar, its coordinates as keywords selecting the
    tuples, none selecting every tuple. A coordinate is part of the key,
    which `add` and `remove` change, and is refused here.

    A property is named `subject.name` - `set("entity.carrier", ...)` -
    and a plain name is an attribute.

    A keyword naming no coordinate of `attribute` is a property of a dim it
    reaches - `ctype="Generator"`, or a list of values - and selects
    the labels of that dim matching it on the record as staged, the
    keywords combining as an intersection; `set` writes one row per label,
    and stores nothing of the filter, so a label added later is not reached.

    Raises
    ------
    KeyError
        On an undeclared attribute or keyword, a label that its dim's
        axis, as staged, does not hold, a tuple that its multi-dim, as
        staged, does not hold, a property's label no layer wrote, or a
        value of a property that refers to a dim and is no
        label of it.
    ValueError
        On a coordinate named as `subject.name`, a keyword the attribute
        does not vary over, a sequence with no single list keyword to align to,
        keys whose coordinate is ambiguous, a label its dim does not
        list, a property keyword whose dim the attribute does not reach
        through exactly one coordinate, or that is given beside that
        coordinate's own keyword, a frame column the schema does not
        declare for `attribute`, or a frame column or label whose type
        does not fit its dtype, timestamps with a time zone among them.

    Notes
    -----
    - [the shape of an edit](https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/design/use/editing/#the-shape-of-an-edit)
    - [set](https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/design/use/editing/#set)
    - [validation](https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/design/use/editing/#validation)
    """
    keyed = isinstance(value, Mapping) or _series_index(value) is not None
    if isinstance(self.schema.resolve(attribute), tuple):
        self._set_dotted(attribute, value, coords)
        return
    coords = self._select(attribute, coords)
    listed = {c: list(v) for c, v in coords.items() if _is_labels(v)}

    if is_frame(value) and not keyed:
        if listed:
            msg = (
                f"`set({attribute!r}, <frame>)` supplies its own keys, so "
                f"keywords {sorted(listed)} may give one label each, not a list"
            )
            raise ValueError(msg)
        call = f"`set({attribute!r}, <frame>)`"
        rel = as_relation(value, self.con)
        self.schema.check_multi_dim_columns(
            self.schema.multi_dims_of(attribute), rel, carrier=call
        )
        self._validate_input(attribute, coords)
        table = self._ensure(_ATTRIBUTES, attribute)
        known = [
            *self._staged_coordinates(attribute),
            *_flat_coordinates(self.schema, attribute),
            "value",
        ]
        extra = sorted(set(rel.columns) - set(known))
        if extra:
            msg = (
                f"{call} was given columns {extra} the schema does not "
                f"declare for {attribute!r}; it takes {sorted(set(known))}"
            )
            raise ValueError(msg)
        rel = self.schema.require_takes(rel, call, attribute=attribute)
        self._insert_long(rel, table, attribute, set(rel.columns), coords)
        return

    self._validate_input(attribute, coords)

    if keyed:
        key = self._key_coordinate(attribute, value, coords)
        keys, values = normalise_value(value)
        dim = _flat_coordinates(self.schema, attribute)[key]
        self._require_typed(
            dim, cast("list[Any]", keys), f"`set({attribute!r}, ...)`"
        )
        column: dict[str, Sequence[Any]] = {key: cast("list[Any]", keys)}
    elif _is_labels(value):
        if len(listed) != 1:
            msg = (
                f"`set({attribute!r}, <sequence>)` aligns to exactly one list "
                f"keyword, and was given {sorted(listed) or 'none'}"
            )
            raise ValueError(msg)
        ((key, labels),) = listed.items()
        del listed[key]
        _, values = normalise_value(value, labels)
        column = {key: labels}
    else:
        values = [value]
        column = {}
    rel = self._values_relation(
        {**column, "value": values},
        {
            **{c: self._coordinate_type(attribute, c) for c in column},
            "value": None,
        },
    )
    for c, labels in listed.items():
        rel = rel.cross(
            self._values_relation(
                {c: labels}, {c: self._coordinate_type(attribute, c)}
            )
        )
    fixed = {c: v for c, v in coords.items() if not _is_labels(v)}
    self._insert_long(
        rel,
        self._ensure(_ATTRIBUTES, attribute),
        attribute,
        set(rel.columns),
        fixed,
    )

def add(
    self,
    dim: str,
    labels: Sequence[Any] | Sequence[Mapping[str, Any]] | DuckDBPyRelation,
    **columns: Any,
) -> None:
    """Stage labels of `dim`, each as one whole row of its axis file.

    `columns` are `dim`'s properties, each a scalar for every label or a
    sequence aligned to `labels`. A column no keyword names is NULL on
    these rows: `add` restates a label's row whole, replacing any this
    record staged for it. A label keeps its place in the axis, a label of
    the base removed here takes its base place back, and a new one is
    appended.

    A multi-dim's labels are tuples, given as a frame holding the struct
    column named for the multi-dim, as `dims[dim]` reads it, or one with a
    column per coordinate instead, or as a list of mappings from
    coordinate to label. A frame may carry property columns too and takes
    a scalar keyword only.

    Not a sequence of `set` calls: a label exists by virtue of its axis row,
    so adding one with no columns at all is an edit. An attribute's value,
    whatever its `dims`, goes through `set`.

    Raises
    ------
    KeyError
        If the schema declares no `dim`, on a value of a property
        that refers to a dim and is no label of it, or on a tuple naming
        a label its coordinate's axis, as staged, does not hold.
    TypeError
        On a frame for a dim that is no multi-dim, or a value that is no
        frame DuckDB rescans.
    ValueError
        On an attribute, a column the axis file has no place for, a
        sequence of the wrong length, a label its dim does not list,
        `dim`'s own included, a label whose type does not fit the dtype
        of `dim`, a tuple missing a coordinate or naming NULL in one, or a
        frame carrying both the struct column and a coordinate column.

    Notes
    -----
    - [add / remove](https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/design/use/editing/#add-remove)
    - [where a value lives](https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/design/storage/format/#where-a-value-lives)
    - [multi-dims](https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/design/model/multi-dims/)
    """
    if dim not in self.schema.dimensions:
        msg = f"the schema declares no dim {dim!r}"
        raise KeyError(msg)
    if dim in self.schema.multi_dims:
        self._add_tuples(dim, labels, columns)
        return
    call = f"add({dim!r}, ...)"
    kind = f"{_AXIS_PREFIX}{dim}"
    names = _plain_labels(dim, labels, f"`{call}`")
    self._reject_undeclared(f"`{call}`", _axis_columns(self.schema, dim), columns)
    self._require_typed(dim, names, f"`{call}`")
    data: dict[str, list[Any]] = {dim: names}
    for c, given in columns.items():
        data[c] = list(given) if _is_labels(given) else [given] * len(names)
        if len(data[c]) != len(names):
            msg = (
                f"`{call}` has {len(data[c])} {c!r} values for {len(names)} labels"
            )
            raise ValueError(msg)
    self.schema.require_listed(dim, data, f"`{call}`")
    self._require_live(dim, data, f"`{call}`")
    rel = self._values_relation(data, {c: self._column_type(c, dim) for c in data})
    table = self._ensure(kind)
    self._insert_snapshot(
        self._positioned(rel, table, kind, dim), table, {}, key=(dim,)
    )

def remove(
    self,
    dim: str,
    labels: Sequence[Any] | Sequence[Mapping[str, Any]] | DuckDBPyRelation,
) -> None:
    """Stage `dim`'s axis without `labels`.

    Need not enumerate what it deletes: the fold drops every value keyed
    by a removed label where `dim` is `partial`. No labels stage nothing.

    And every multi-dim with a coordinate over `dim` without the tuples
    naming one of `labels`, read from the record as it currently resolves:
    a multi-dim attribute's value goes with its tuple.

    A multi-dim's labels are tuples, given as `add` takes them.

    Raises
    ------
    TypeError
        As `add` does.
    ValueError
        On a label whose type does not fit the dtype of `dim`, a tuple
        given as `add` refuses it, or while a property
        that refers to `dim` stores one of `labels` in the record as
        staged.

    Notes
    -----
    - [add / remove](https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/design/use/editing/#add-remove)
    - [deletion](https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/design/layers/removal/)
    """
    call = f"`remove({dim!r}, ...)`"
    if dim in self.schema.multi_dims:
        if not is_frame(labels) and not labels:
            return
        rel = self._tuples(dim, self._tuple_frame(dim, labels, {}, call), call)
        table = self._ensure(f"{_AXIS_PREFIX}{dim}")
        self._delete(table, rel, dim, col(table, dim))
        return
    labels = _plain_labels(dim, labels, call)
    if not labels:
        return
    self._require_typed(dim, labels, call)
    self._require_unnamed(dim, labels)
    gone = self._values_relation({dim: list(labels)}, {dim: self._column_type(dim)})
    staged = self.dims
    for m in self.schema.multi_dims:
        fields = [f for f, d in self.schema.over(m).items() if d == dim]
        if not fields or m not in staged:
            continue
        naming = reduce(
            operator.or_,
            (
                fn.struct_extract(col(m), lit(f)).isin(*map(lit, labels))
                for f in fields
            ),
        )
        if staged[m].filter(naming).limit(1).fetchone() is None:
            continue
        table = self._ensure(f"{_AXIS_PREFIX}{m}")
        for f in fields:
            self._delete(table, gone, dim, fn.struct_extract(col(table, m), lit(f)))
    table = self._ensure(f"{_AXIS_PREFIX}{dim}")
    self._delete(table, gone, dim, col(table, dim))

def rollback(self) -> None:
    """Clear every staged row without writing.

    Notes
    -----
    - [WorkingRecord](https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/design/use/editing/)

    for name in self._staged.values():

    self._staged.clear()

def coordinates_of(self, attribute: str) -> tuple[str, ...]:
    """The coordinate columns one attribute's rows carry, multi-dims first.

    A multi-dim in `dims` is carried as one struct column named for it, so
    `dims={"connection", "snapshot"}` gives `("connection", "snapshot")`.

    Per attribute rather than schema-wide: one file per attribute means one
    column set per attribute, and an all-NULL column of a dim the attribute
    is not addressed by would claim a coordinate the value has none of.

    Notes
    -----
    - [multi-dims](https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/design/model/multi-dims/)
    - [addressing](https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/design/model/multi-dims/#attributes-over-a-multi-dim)
    - [the long schema](https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/design/storage/format/#the-long-schema)
    """
    spec = self.attributes.get(attribute)
    if spec is None:
        return ()
    return (
        *self.multi_dims_of(attribute),
        *(d for d in self.dims if d in spec.dims),
    )

def duck_type(self, spec: Dimension | AttributeSpec | PropertySpec) -> DuckDBPyType:
    """Return the DuckDB type of a declared dim, attribute or property.

    A dim with `one_of` has the `ENUM` of them, a multi-dim the struct of
    a field per coordinate, typed as the dim it draws on. A property that
    refers to a dim has the type of that dim.

    Notes
    -----
    - [dtypes](https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/design/model/schema/#dtypes)
    - [multi-dims](https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/design/model/multi-dims/)
    """
    if isinstance(spec, PropertySpec) and spec.one_of is not None:
        return self.duck_type(self.dimensions[spec.one_of])
    if isinstance(spec, Dimension) and spec.over is not None:
        return duckdb.struct_type(
            {c: self.duck_type(self.dimensions[d]) for c, d in spec.over.items()}
        )
    if isinstance(spec, Dimension) and spec.one_of is not None:
        return enum_type(spec.one_of)
    return DUCK_TYPES[cast("str", spec.dtype)]

def check_multi_dim_columns(
    self,
    multi_dims: Iterable[str],
    rel: DuckDBPyRelation,
    *,
    carrier: str,
) -> None:
    """Reject each of `multi_dims` carried other than as one struct column of exactly its coordinates, whole or NULL.

    A carrier without a multi-dim's column passes.

    Parameters
    ----------
    carrier
        What carries the columns, named in the message.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        On a coordinate as a column of its own, a multi-dim column not a
        struct of exactly the coordinates, naming the struct to pass
        instead, or a struct with some fields NULL and not all.

    Notes
    -----
    - [multi-dims](https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/design/model/multi-dims/)
    - [the broadcast rule](https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/design/model/attributes/#the-broadcast-rule)
    """
    types = dict(zip(rel.columns, rel.types, strict=True))
    for multi in multi_dims:
        key = list(self.over(multi))
        flat = [c for c in key if c in types]
        dtype = types.get(multi)
        fields = (
            key
            if dtype is None
            else [name for name, _ in dtype.children]
            if dtype.id == "struct"
            else None
        )
        if flat or fields is None or set(fields) != set(key):
            carried = f"{flat} flat" if flat else f"{multi!r} as {dtype}"
            msg = (
                f"{carrier} carries {carried}; pass {multi!r} as one struct "
                f"column with a field per coordinate, {key} (https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/design/model/multi-dims/)"
            )
            raise ValueError(msg)
        if dtype is None:
            continue
        some = " OR ".join(
            f"{fn.struct_extract(col(multi), lit(c))} IS NULL" for c in key
        )
        partly = sql(f"{col(multi)} IS NOT NULL AND ({some})")
        if rel.filter(partly).limit(1).fetchone() is not None:
            msg = (
                f"{carrier} carries a {multi!r} with some fields NULL; a "
                f"multi-dim value is a whole tuple, or NULL for every tuple (https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/design/model/attributes/#the-broadcast-rule)"
            )
            raise ValueError(msg)

def long_columns_for(self, attribute: str) -> tuple[str, ...]:
    """Return one attribute's full long column set, in order.

    An attribute carries the coordinates its `dims` name and no others, so a
    per-snapshot weighting has no column for any other dim.

    KeyError
        If the schema does not declare `attribute`.

    Notes
    -----
    - [the long schema](https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/design/storage/format/#the-long-schema)
    """
    if attribute not in self.attributes:
        msg = f"the schema declares no attribute {attribute!r}"

def categorizing(self, dim: str) -> tuple[str, ...]:
    """Return the categorizing properties of `dim`, the ones `default_by` keys on.

    A categorizing property is a property of `dim` that refers to a dim with
    `one_of`. Only a dim in `partial` that is no multi-dim has any.

    Notes
    -----
    - [categories](https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/design/model/properties/#categories)
    """
    if dim not in self.dims or dim not in (self.partial or set()):
        return ()
    return tuple(
        name
        for name, spec in self.properties.get(dim, {}).items()
        if spec.one_of is not None
        and self.dimensions[spec.one_of].one_of is not None
    )

def require_listed(
    self, subject: str, data: Mapping[str, Iterable[Any]], what: str
) -> None:
    """Refuse a label its dim does not list.

    `data` maps column names to values. A name is checked where it is
    `subject` and `subject` has `one_of`, or where it is a property of
    `subject` that refers to a dim with `one_of`. Other names
    and NULL values are skipped.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        Naming `what`, the column, the unknown labels and the dim's
        `one_of` labels.

    Notes
    -----
    - [dtypes](https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/design/model/schema/#dtypes)
    """
    specs = self.properties.get(subject, {})
    for name, values in data.items():
        if name in specs:
            listed = self._listed(specs[name])
        elif name == subject and subject in self.dimensions:
            listed = self._listed(self.dimensions[subject])
        else:
            continue
        if listed is None:
            continue
        unknown = sorted({str(v) for v in values if v is not None} - {*listed})
        if unknown:
            msg = (
                f"{what} gives {name!r} labels {unknown}, which its dim's "
                f"`one_of` does not hold; `one_of` is {list(listed)}"
            )
            raise ValueError(msg)

def default_for(self, name: str, **categories: str) -> Any:
    """The default of attribute or `subject.name` property `name` for a label of `categories`.

    `categories` are keyed by each categorizing property's own name. The
    first `default_by` key listing the label's category decides, else
    `default`; a category left out matches none.

    Raises
    ------
    KeyError
        As `resolve` does, and on a coordinate, which has no default.

    Notes
    -----
    - [AttributeSpec](https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/design/model/attributes/#attributespec)
    - [default_by](https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/design/model/properties/#default_by-a-default-per-category)
    """
    resolved = self.resolve(name)
    spec = resolved[1] if isinstance(resolved, tuple) else resolved
    if isinstance(spec, Dimension):
        msg = f"{name!r} is a coordinate, part of its multi-dim's key, and has no default"
        raise KeyError(msg)
    for key, by in spec.default_by.items():
        category = categories.get(key.partition(".")[2])
        if category in by:
            return by[category]
    return spec.default

def addresses(self, attribute: str, dim: str) -> bool:
    """Whether `attribute` reaches a label of `dim` at all.

    True where its `dims` name `dim`, or a multi-dim one of whose
    coordinates draws on `dim`.

    Notes
    -----

    """
    spec = self.attributes.get(attribute)
    return (spec is not None and dim in spec.dims) or any(
        dim in self.over(m).values() for m in self.multi_dims_of(attribute)
    )

def resolve(
    self, name: str
) -> AttributeSpec | tuple[str, PropertySpec] | tuple[str, Dimension]:
    """What `name` addresses: an attribute, or a property or coordinate as `subject.name`.

    Read off the name alone: a plain name is never a property.

    Returns
    -------
    AttributeSpec or tuple of str and PropertySpec or Dimension
        The attribute's spec, a property's subject and spec, or a
        coordinate's multi-dim and the dim the coordinate draws on.

    Raises
    ------
    KeyError
        If `name` addresses nothing; for a plain name some subject's
        property is called, naming each dotted form.

    Notes
    -----
    - [properties](https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/design/model/properties/#properties)
    - [coordinates](https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/design/model/multi-dims/#coordinates)
    """
    subject, dot, prop = name.partition(".")
    if dot:
        spec = self.properties.get(subject, {}).get(prop)
        if spec is not None:
            return subject, spec
        drawn = self.over(subject).get(prop) if subject in self.dimensions else None
        if drawn is None:
            msg = f"the schema declares no property {name!r}"
            raise KeyError(msg)
        return subject, self.dimensions[drawn]
    attribute = self.attributes.get(name)
    if attribute is not None:
        return attribute
    dotted = sorted(
        f"`{s}.{name}`" for s, specs in self.properties.items() if name in specs
    )
    hint = f"; did you mean {' or '.join(dotted)}" if dotted else ""
    msg = f"the schema declares no attribute {name!r}{hint}"
    raise KeyError(msg)

def coordinate_over(self, multi: str, dim: str) -> str | None:
    """The one coordinate of the multi-dim `multi` drawing on `dim`, if any.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If several coordinates of `multi` draw on `dim`.
    """
    fields = [f for f, d in self.over(multi).items() if d == dim]
    if len(fields) > 1:
        msg = (
            f"multi-dim {multi!r} is over {dim!r} through {fields}, so no one "
            f"label of it decides what a tuple carries"
        )
        raise ValueError(msg)
    return fields[0] if fields else None

def owned_per(self, attribute: str) -> frozenset[str]:
    """Which dims a layer owns `attribute` per.

    Derived rather than declared: `AttributeSpec.dims` says which axes the
    attribute may vary over, `partial_dims` the fold key (the `partial`
    dims, multi-dims among them), and ownership is their intersection. A
    dim in `dims` but not the fold key - a non-`partial` value axis like
    `timestep` - is owned whole, so a patch to one of its values restates the
    attribute's entire extent along it (`_owned_whole`).

    Notes
    -----
    - [partial](https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/design/layers/tree/#partial-the-granularity-of-an-override)
    - [one fold for every axis](https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/design/layers/resolution/#one-fold-for-every-axis)
    """
    spec = self.attributes.get(attribute)
    if spec is None:
        return frozenset()
    return spec.dims & set(self.partial_dims)

def column_type(
    self, column: str, subject: str | None = None
) -> DuckDBPyType | None:
    """Return the declared DuckDB type of `column`, or None if the schema declares none.

    Covers the structural columns the format fixes, the declared dims,
    multi-dims among them, the properties of `subject` - columns of its
    axis file, read first - and the owner map's two flag structs, whose fields
    follow the schema's dims.

    No dim is structural: each is declared, and typed from that
    declaration. So the `ENUM` of a dim with `one_of` pins them
    everywhere the column is built. An attribute is no column but a long row's value,
    typed by `value_type`.

    A schema declaring no dims at all is "no manifest yet" rather
    than a record to fold, and DuckDB has no empty struct - so the flag
    columns are undeclared there, and a caller building an empty relation
    falls back to `VARCHAR` for a map that will never hold a row.

    Notes
    -----
    - [one schema per record](https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/design/model/schema/#one-schema-per-record)
    - [the owner map](https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/design/layers/resolution/#owner-map)
    """
    found = self.declared(column, subject)
    return None if found is None else found[1]

def declared(
    self, column: str, subject: str | None = None, attribute: str | None = None
) -> tuple[str, DuckDBPyType, str] | None:
    """Look up the declaration of `column`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    subject
        The dim whose file holds the column. A column named like
        one of its properties is that property, named `subject.name`.
    attribute
        The attribute whose long rows hold the column. Its `value` column
        is the attribute, named as it is.

    Returns
    -------
    tuple of str, DuckDBPyType and str, or None
        The declared name, the DuckDB type, and the dtype as an error
        message shows it; None where the schema declares no type for
        `column`.

    Notes
    -----
    - [dtypes](https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/design/model/schema/#dtypes)
    """
    own = self.properties.get(subject or "", {})
    spec: Dimension | AttributeSpec | PropertySpec
    if attribute is not None and column == "value":
        name, spec = attribute, self.attributes[attribute]
    elif column in own:
        name, spec = f"{subject}.{column}", own[column]
    elif column in self.dimensions and column not in STRUCTURAL_TYPES:
        name, spec = column, self.dimensions[column]
    else:
        duck = self._structural_type(column)
        return None if duck is None else (column, duck, str(duck))
    duck = self.duck_type(spec)
    return name, duck, f"{_typed_as(spec)} ({duck})"

Check that each column of rel has a type that fits its declaration, and return rel, with its all-NULL columns cast to their declared types.

A column type fits where takes says so. A column that fails this but holds only NULLs passes and is cast to its declared type, because dataframe libraries guess the type of an empty or all-None column. Only such columns have their rows read. subject and attribute are as in declared.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

Naming what, and for each refused column its type, its declared name and its dtype.

Notes

  • set
Source code in src/datarecord/schema/schema.py 
def require_takes(
    self,
    rel: DuckDBPyRelation,
    what: str,
    subject: str | None = None,
    attribute: str | None = None,
) -> DuckDBPyRelation:
    """Check that each column of `rel` has a type that fits its declaration, and return `rel`, with its all-NULL columns cast to their declared types.

    A column type fits where `takes` says so. A column
    that fails this but holds only NULLs passes and is cast to its declared
    type, because dataframe libraries guess the type of an empty or
    all-None column. Only such columns have their rows read. `subject` and
    `attribute` are as in `declared`.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        Naming `what`, and for each refused column its type, its
        declared name and its dtype.

    Notes
    -----
    - [dtypes](https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/design/model/schema/#dtypes)
    - [set](https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/design/use/editing/#set)
    """
    wrong = []
    nulls: dict[str, DuckDBPyType] = {}
    for c, given in zip(rel.columns, rel.types, strict=True):
        found = self.declared(c, subject, attribute)
        if found is None or takes(found[1], given):
            continue
        if rel.filter(col(c).isnotnull()).limit(1).fetchone() is None:
            nulls[c] = found[1]
            continue
        name, _, shown = found
        wrong.append(
            f"column {c!r} has type {given}, which does not fit {name!r} "
            f"of dtype {shown}"
        )
    if wrong:
        msg = f"{what}: {'; '.join(wrong)}"
        raise ValueError(msg)
    if not nulls:
        return rel
    return rel.project(
        *(
            col(c).cast(nulls[c]).alias(c) if c in nulls else col(c)
            for c in rel.columns
        )
    )

def compatible_with(self, other: Schema) -> list[str]:
    """Why layers written under `other` would not read under `self`.

    Empty when the change is compatible: old layers stay readable and only
    `version` moves. The compatible changes are those where NULL already
    means what the new schema needs it to mean, so the broadcast rule absorbs
    them without touching a row.

    Returns
    -------
    list of str
        One reason per incompatibility, empty if there are none.

    Notes
    -----
    - [the broadcast rule](https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/design/model/attributes/#the-broadcast-rule)
    - [versioning](https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/design/model/schema/#versioning)
    """
    problems = []

    for dim, was in other.dimensions.items():
        now = self.dimensions.get(dim)
        if now is None:
            problems.append(f"dim {dim!r} removed")
            continue
        if _typed_as(now) != _typed_as(was):
            problems.append(f"dim {dim!r} {_typed_as(was)} -> {_typed_as(now)}")

    for attr, was_spec in other.attributes.items():
        now_spec = self.attributes.get(attr)
        if now_spec is None:
            problems.append(f"attribute {attr!r} removed")
            continue
        if now_spec.dtype != was_spec.dtype:
            problems.append(
                f"attribute {attr!r} dtype {was_spec.dtype} -> {now_spec.dtype}"
            )
        narrowed = was_spec.dims - now_spec.dims
        if narrowed:
            problems.append(
                f"attribute {attr!r} no longer varies over {sorted(narrowed)}; "
                f"rows setting those dims have no valid reading"
            )

    for dim, specs in other.properties.items():
        for name, was_prop in specs.items():
            now_prop = self.properties.get(dim, {}).get(name)
            if now_prop is None:
                problems.append(f"property {name!r} of {dim!r} removed")
            elif _typed_as(now_prop) != _typed_as(was_prop):
                problems.append(
                    f"property {name!r} of {dim!r} {_typed_as(was_prop)} "
                    f"-> {_typed_as(now_prop)}"
                )

    if other.partial is not None and self.partial is not None:
        lost = other.partial - self.partial
        if lost:
            problems.append(
                f"{sorted(lost)} no longer `partial`; a layer that patched one "
                f"value along such an axis is now a partial override of an axis "
                f"owned whole"
            )
    return problems

def files(self, uri: str) -> Files:
    """The `Files` for `uri`'s scheme: local without `://`, remote for `s3://`.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        For any other scheme.
    """

    if not uri.startswith("s3://"):
        msg = f"{uri}: a location is a local path or an s3:// URI"
        raise ValueError(msg)
    with self._remote_lock:
        if self._remote is None:
            self._remote = self._connect_remote()
        return self._remote

def at(self, uri: str) -> Record:
    """The standalone record at `uri`, read under its own `manifest.json`.

    A local `uri` is resolved, as `store` resolves one, so a later `chdir`
    cannot point it at another record.

    Raises
    ------
    FileNotFoundError
        If `uri` has no manifest: a directory without one is a tree layer,
        read under its store's schema through `Store.layer`.
    ValueError
        If the manifest carries no record id.

    Notes
    -----
    - [the record format](https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/design/storage/format/)
    - [one schema per record](https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/design/model/schema/#one-schema-per-record)
    """
    base = _absolute(uri) + "/"
    found = self.files(base).read_text(base + "manifest.json")
    if found is None:
        msg = (
            f"{base} has no manifest.json; a layer of a tree is read through "
            f"its store's `layer(id)`"
        )
        raise FileNotFoundError(msg)
    schema = Schema.model_validate_json(found[0])
    if schema.id is None:
        msg = (
            f"{base}manifest.json carries no record id; a standalone "
            f"record's id is minted by `Workspace.write`, so write it again "
            f"through that"
        )
        raise ValueError(msg)
    source = DirectorySource(base, schema, self, schema.id)
    return Record(schema.id, [source], self, schema)

def write(self, source: LayerData | RecordLike, uri: str) -> Record:
    """Write `source` as a standalone record at `uri`, and read it back.

    A standalone record is written to a URI that does not exist yet. The
    directory carries its own manifest, written last, so one whose write
    failed reads as no record. The manifest carries a fresh id, so a
    record written again at `uri` is never read as the one before it.

    Raises
    ------
    FileExistsError
        If anything exists at `uri`: locally the path, even an empty
        directory; remotely any key under it.

    Notes
    -----
    - [writing a whole record](https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/design/use/writing/)
    - [a standalone directory](https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/design/storage/concurrency/#a-standalone-directory)
    """
    base = _absolute(uri) + "/"
    if self.files(base).exists(base):
        msg = (
            f"{base} already exists; a standalone record is written to a URI "
            f"that does not exist yet"
        )
        raise FileExistsError(msg)
    data = layer_data(source, self.con)
    write_layer(data, base, self, manifest=_manifest(data.schema, uuid4()))
    return self.at(base)

Look one revision up, reading its file and any parents not yet held.

Type Description KeyError

Source code in src/datarecord/store/store.py 
def revision(self, id: UUID) -> Revision:
    """Look one revision up, reading its file and any parents not yet held.

    Raises
    ------
    KeyError
        If this store has no revision `id`.

    Notes
    -----
    - [the tree beside the layers](https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/design/storage/store/#the-tree-beside-the-layers)
    """
    row = self._held(id)
    if row is None:
        read = []
        next_id: UUID | None = id
        while next_id is not None and self._held(next_id) is None:
            found = self._read_revision(next_id)
            if found is None:
                msg = f"No revision {next_id} in {self.uri}"
                raise KeyError(msg)
            read.append(found)
            next_id = found[1]
        self._cache(read)
        row = read[0]
    return Revision(id=row[0], parent=row[1], store=self)

def revisions(self) -> list[Revision]:
    """Every revision in this store, unordered.

    One listing of `revisions/`, reading only the files the workspace does
    not already hold.

    Notes
    -----
    - [the tree beside the layers](https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/design/storage/store/#the-tree-beside-the-layers)
    """
    held = {
        row[0]
        for row in self.workspace.con.execute(
            "SELECT id FROM revisions WHERE location = ?", [self.uri]
        ).fetchall()
    }
    listed = {
        UUID(name.removesuffix(".json"))
        for name in self.files.list(f"{self.uri}/revisions/")
        if name.endswith(".json")
    }
    self._cache(
        [
            row
            for id in listed - held
            if (row := self._read_revision(id)) is not None
        ]
    )
    rows = self.workspace.con.execute(
        "SELECT id, parent FROM revisions WHERE location = ?", [self.uri]
    ).fetchall()
    return [Revision(id=id, parent=parent, store=self) for id, parent in rows]

def layer(self, id: UUID) -> Record:
    """Revision `id`'s layer read alone, as the one layer it is.

    Under this store's schema: a layer holds only data. Not the revision's
    record - nothing beneath it is folded in.
    """
    # Not `id`, whose fold tables hold the whole ancestry's fold.
    layer_id = uuid5(id, "layer")
    schema = read_schema(self)
    source = DirectorySource(self.layer_dir(id), schema, self.workspace, layer_id)
    return Record(layer_id, [source], self.workspace, schema)

def child(self, source: LayerData | RecordLike) -> Revision:
    """A new child of this revision, with `source` as its layer.

    Any node may be a parent: a layer is write-once, so a base cannot shift
    under its descendants. A `WorkingRecord`'s `edits` are a delta against
    the revision it was built over, so they are written only under that
    one; the `WorkingRecord` itself writes its whole resolved record.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If `source` is staged edits built over another revision, whose delta
        would read back wrong here.

    Notes
    -----
    - [a layer's data is write-once](https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/design/layers/tree/#a-layers-data-is-write-once)
    - [writing a whole record](https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/design/use/writing/)
    - [edits](https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/design/use/editing/#edits)
    """
    if isinstance(source, StagedSource) and source.base != self.id:
        msg = (
            f"these edits were staged over revision {source.base}, so they "
            f"are a delta against it and not against {self.id}; write them "
            f"as a child of the revision the `WorkingRecord` was built over"
        )
        raise ValueError(msg)
    return self.store._write(source, self.id)

def materialise(self) -> None:
    """Write this node's caches - owner maps and resolved dims.

    A policy rather than a lifecycle step, and purely additive: it changes
    no answer, only how many layers a descendant's read touches. Once these
    exist, a read stops here instead of walking further up.

    Notes

    - [materialised node caches](https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/design/layers/resolution/#materialised-node-caches)
    """
    materialise(self.id, self.record.sources, self.store)
    self._record = None

Requirements(
    dims: frozenset[str] = frozenset(),
    categories: frozenset[str] = frozenset(),
    attributes: frozenset[tuple[str, str]] = frozenset(),
    unsupported_keys: frozenset[
        tuple[str, str]

    ] = frozenset(),

    ignored: frozenset[tuple[str, str]] = frozenset(),
)

What a tool needs from a record, and what a given record fails to supply.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default dims frozenset of str

Dims the tool cannot build a model without.

frozenset() categories frozenset of str

Categories the tool requires the record to define labels of, or, in a verify result, ones it has no counterpart for.

frozenset() attributes frozenset of tuple of (str, str)

(category, attribute) pairs: an attribute the tool requires a value for on the labels of that category. Named in the record's vocabulary, not the tool's, so a caller can act on them: an attribute the tool renames or computes (Schema) is reported by the source attribute it is missing.

frozenset() unsupported_keys frozenset of tuple of (str, str)

(key, dim) pairs the schema declares that this tool cannot honour; key is "owner_map_key", the fold's unit of ownership. The record layer trusts every declared key, so this is a tool's verdict on the record it was handed, not a schema rejection.

frozenset() unsupported_values frozenset of tuple of (str, str)

(category, attribute) pairs whose stored shape this tool cannot represent, as opposed to a value it is missing - a piecewise-linear attribute where the tool takes a scalar.

frozenset() names frozenset of str

Labels the framework scopes per category and two of its categories claim, where a record has one axis row per label.

frozenset() columns frozenset of tuple of (str, str)

(category, column) pairs of a framework's own column whose name the record declares with another shape, so it has nowhere to be stored: one name is one spec record-wide.

frozenset() ignored frozenset of tuple of (str, str)

(category, attribute) pairs the record stores a value for that the tool's category does not take, so the build leaves it out. A report, not a failure: it leaves the result falsy and describe silent.

frozenset() Notes
  • wide and long rows
  • a label is unique within its dim
  • consuming a record

Source code in src/datarecord/tools/base.py 
def describe(self) -> str:
    """A one-line summary, for an error message or a log line."""
    parts = []
    if self.dims:
        parts.append(f"dims {sorted(self.dims)}")
    if self.categories:
        parts.append(f"categories {sorted(self.categories)}")
    if self.attributes:
        parts.append(f"attributes {sorted(self.attributes)}")
    if self.unsupported_keys:
        unsupported = ", ".join(
            f"{dim} as {key}" for key, dim in sorted(self.unsupported_keys)
        )
        parts.append(f"unsupported keys ({unsupported})")
    if self.unsupported_values:
        parts.append(
            f"piecewise-linear attributes {sorted(self.unsupported_values)}"
        )
    if self.names:
        parts.append(
            f"labels claimed by more than one category "
            f"{sorted(self.names)} (https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/design/storage/format/#a-label-is-unique-within-its-dim)"
        )
    if self.columns:
        parts.append(
            f"columns whose name is declared with another shape "
            f"{sorted(self.columns)}"
        )
    return ", ".join(parts) if parts else "nothing"

def resolve(
    self,
    record: RecordLike,
    labels: Mapping[str, DuckDBPyRelation],
    flags: Mapping[str, Flags],
    *,
    filter: bool = True,
) -> DuckDBPyRelation:
    """This attribute's long relation, each source settled (`settle`) before `compute`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    flags
        Per source, its `Flags` as `settle` takes them.
    filter
        As `settle` takes it.

    Notes
    -----
    - [the Record protocol](https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/design/use/reading/)
    - [settling rows](https://energy-models.github.io/datarecord/design/use/reading/#settling-rows)
    """
    rels = [
        settle(record.attributes[s], labels, flags[s], filter=filter)
        for s in self.source
    ]
    if self.compute is None:
        return rels[0]
    return self.compute(*rels)

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Status: Draft · Owner: Jonas Hörsch · Date: 2026-08-05

A record holds labeled data with a declared schema. Its labels sit on axes called dims. A multi-dim is a dim whose labels are tuples of other dims' labels, listing which combinations exist. Properties describe single labels, and attributes hold values at coordinates. The schema declares what may exist, and the data says what does. A record can be one parquet directory or a tree of layers, and a reader reads both through one interface. The package depends on DuckDB, pydantic and mathspec, and names no modelling framework.

These pages are the authoritative design. Usage shows how to use the package. Docstrings in the source cite these pages by link.

docs.title: The parts of a record
docs.text:
A dim is an axis: a set of unique labels, such as the buses of a network or its snapshots. A dim with one_of fixes which labels it may hold.

A multi-dim is a dim whose labels are tuples of other dims' labels. It declares which tuples exist, such as which entity attaches to which bus.

A property holds one value per label of a dim and describes that label, such as the carrier of a generator. A property can refer back to another dimension using one_of.

An attribute holds values at coordinates over the dims it names, such as a generator's available output per snapshot, or the resulting dispatch of the solution.

The schema declares the dims, properties and attributes with their dtypes. The data says which labels, tuples and values exist.

A RecordLike object exposes each of them, and returns dims, properties and attributes as DuckDB relations. The reading page defines the protocol in full.

record.schema                   what may exist: the axes, properties, attributes
record.dims                     the axes themselves, multi-dims included, keyed by dim
record.properties               what describes each label, keyed by dim
record.attributes               the values, results included, keyed by attribute name
record.flags(**cats)            which axes an attribute actually uses

docs.title: The running example
docs.text: The pages illustrate the design with one example schema, shaped like PyPSA's (the PyPSA tool). Its dims are entity, bus, carrier, snapshot and ctype. The properties entity.ctype and entity.carrier refer back to their dimension. ctype is a dim with one_of, whose labels are component classes such as Generator, Link and Load, so an attribute over entity can have a default per ctype. The multi-dim connection lists the (entity, bus) tuples that exist, and attributes such as p_nom and p_max_pu hold values over entity and snapshot. The schema declares each of these names like any other.

docs.title: Core interface
docs.text:
Record is the one class that implements the protocol. It reads a fold across layers:

  • A tree of layers, each adding a partial record on top of its parent, a deeper layer's row winning where it crosses a shallower one. Revision.record gives one (a tree of layers).
  • One parquet directory, through Workspace.at(uri). It folds as a tree with one layer, which degenerates to a scan of it.
  • A WorkingRecord, whose last layer stages edits, so pending edits read back before anything is written.

A framework's own object may satisfy RecordLike too, such as a PyPSA Network that presents itself as a record and depends on nothing in this package. A consumer cannot tell which kind it holds, so a framework reads a hundred-layer tree through the same calls as a single directory.

A framework consumes a record, a workflow engine produces one, and neither needs to know how the other works. datarecord depends on duckdb, pydantic and mathspec, whose dtypes a schema declares. Its optional datarecord[remote] adds boto3 for a location on S3 (files, local and remote). A framework's tool lives under datarecord/tools/ behind its own extra (the package).

docs.title: Scope
docs.text:
The design covers the RecordLike protocol and WorkingRecord, the data model and its schema, layers and their resolution, the write path, and the parquet format that stores a record.

Out of scope are an implementation on an engine other than DuckDB (one engine) and layers that are not materialised as parquet. Concurrent writers to one record meet only at the manifest (concurrent writers).

docs.title: The pages
