• Per-bus patching needs bus in partial. bus is no membership key any more, so a layer patching a per-bus marginal_price one bus at a time declares it partial like any value dim; a connection's bus is patched per row regardless, inside connection.
  • A value staged without bus= matches no connection. It is stored keyed {entity, NULL}, and a NULL field compares equal only to a NULL field. The "every connection of this entity" reading the pages gave was never implemented; it is left open.
  • The entity tombstone reaches the entity inside the struct. The fold matches it on every entity a row names — entity, and each key coordinate over entity of a keyed group — so removing an entity drops its connections' values as before, the tuples standing until removed in turn. A first cut had remove tombstone every tuple naming the entity instead, which left a re-added entity without its parent's connections.
  • A layer's own tombstones apply only to its parents. So the staged collapse drops its own rows itself: remove_group also drops the rows it staged on the tuple, as remove does on the entity.
  • A long frame handed to set carries the struct only. Accepting its coordinates flat as well cost a second packing path and a both-forms rejection for no caller that needed it: the PyPSA tool packs once, where it builds its frames.
  • An empty frame must still type the group column as the struct. A source emitting no rows for an attribute hands over a typed empty relation, or the writer rejects a column that is not a struct of the group's key.
  • Shadowing went. A group sharing a dim's name was resolved to the dim, which every place that tells a group column from a dim had to repeat. Once a group is a column named for itself, the collision is two columns under one name, so the schema rejects it; only the entity-type group, which never becomes a column, keeps its dim's name.
  • A flat group file cost a conversion wherever a row met it. The fold's group tombstones, the staged collapse, remove_group and add each packed the file's coordinates into the struct. Keying groups/<group>.parquet by its struct column, as an axis file is keyed by its dim, removed every one; packing survives only where a caller hands flat values in — set's coordinate keywords, remove_group's tuples, add's wide frame — and in the PyPSA tool, whose network is flat.
  • PyPSA's bus was an attribute and a coordinate at once. The tool declared the port stem bus as an attribute over connection, which in a flat file was the same column as the coordinate. Under the struct it would be a second column beside the key, so the tool declares no such attribute: a port's bus is the connection tuple, and a component with no connection row lacks it whatever default PyPSA registers.

docs.title: Amendment: a group is a dim
docs.text:
Status: Implemented · Drafted 2026-10-13 · Implemented 2026-10-13

As for the proposal above, the schema, record, read-path and working-record pages are authoritative; what the implementation found records where it departs.

Once a group is one column, the reasons it stayed a membership key, apart from the dims, are gone. A group is a dim whose axis is the resolved group: groups/<group>.parquet, keyed by the column named for the group, as dims/<dim>.parquet is. It broadcasts, enters the owner map only where partial names it, and is owned whole otherwise — the rules snapshot follows, unchanged.

docs.title: A group value is a whole tuple or NULL
docs.text: A struct is either complete or NULL as a whole; {entity: dc, bus: NULL} is no value. A NULL struct means every tuple of the group, by the broadcast rule, expanded against the resolved group as a NULL dim is against its axis. A partly NULL struct is refused wherever a row comes in — set's keywords and frames, add_group, and the writer — since it would name a tuple no group row matches. This replaces "a group column does not broadcast" above, whose reason was that only the group's table knows its tuples; the fold has that table already (Coords.groups).

docs.title: The owner map
docs.text:
The membership key is entity alone, and a group is keyed exactly where a dim is: in partial_dims if partial names it, absent otherwise.

# inputs
entity        -- NULL on a row over a group, which names its entities inside it
<partial dims, groups among them>
attribute
layer_uuid
varies        STRUCT(<broadcast coordinate>: BOOLEAN, ...)   -- a field per group too
broadcast     STRUCT(<broadcast coordinate>: BOOLEAN, ...)
breakpoints   BOOLEAN

Only the groups a long input row can carry are keyed goes, and Schema.group_columns with it: which coordinates key the map is partial's to say, for a group as for a dim.

Not partial, a layer writes the attribute's whole extent along the group. A connection attribute carries no top-level entity, so its key is (attribute), and a layer touching {steel_dri, h2_north} owns every connection's value — the granularity an attribute over {snapshot} alone, a weighting, has today. Staging carries the rest of the extent, as it does for a non-partial dim (_complete_owned_whole); a layer written directly has to hold it. Pulling the struct's entity fields out into the key would narrow that to one entity's connections, at the price of the map reaching into struct fields; not worth it, since partial gives the finer grain where a tool wants it.

partial, a layer patches one tuple. The group is in the key, a NULL struct expands against the resolved group in the fold, and a group tombstone anti-joins the parent on it, as a partial dim's does on its axis. The PyPSA tool declares connection partial: Link.efficiency may vary over snapshot, and restating every link's series to patch one is the cost partial exists to avoid.

docs.title: What it costs
docs.text:
• flags(ctype) cannot scope a non-partial group attribute. Its map rows name no entity, so no type claims them — the position an axis-only attribute is in today, and the record-level flags question widens from a corner to every such attribute. With connection partial, PyPSA's are unaffected.
  • An owner-map format change, materialised maps rebuilt; pre-1.0, no reader for the old key survives.
  • The default grain coarsens. A schema that relied on per-connection ownership without saying so now says partial={"connection"}.

docs.title: What it saves
docs.text:
The struct change left src/ about 340 lines larger than the flat layout it replaced, most of it in packing, validation and the PyPSA tool's conversion, which this does not touch. What goes is the group's separate path through the key:

goes comes group_columns, and the derivation of which groups are keyed broadcast_dims naming groups, the entity-type group excepted group columns as a second key family in membership_keys, long_columns, fold_inputs' padding and projection expand_dims taking a group's relation where it takes an axis the group-tombstone membership in fold_inputs, separate from the partial dims' a partial coordinate's tombstone reading source.group(g) for a group the docs' account of which groups are keyed and why the whole-or-NULL check at the three entry points

It was estimated at 40–80 lines net out of src/. Measured, it saved none: src/ grew by 19 lines net (119 added, 100 removed). The derivation of keyed groups and membership_keys went as planned, and three things the estimate did not foresee added back as much — the read-time entity filter, the attribute-scoped expansion and the whole-or-NULL check against data rather than dtypes. The "which groups are keyed" sections of the design pages went. The gain is one rule where there were two: everything said of a dim — broadcast, partial, owned whole, flags — is said of a group, with the group's file as its axis.

docs.title: Landing
docs.text:
1. Schema: groups among the broadcast coordinates; membership_keys is entity; partial may name a group; group_columns goes.
  2. The fold: expand_dims over a group's relation; a partial group's tombstone; the flags gain a field per group.
  3. The whole-or-NULL check in staging and the writer; set stages a NULL struct where no coordinate is given.
  4. The PyPSA tool declares connection partial.
  5. Schema, record, read-path and working-record pages; the open question widened.

docs.title: What the amendment found
docs.text:
• A NULL is expanded only for the attributes over its coordinate. The fold key is one tuple over every attribute, so an attribute not over connection holds NULL there for want of the column; expanding every NULL multiplied its rows by the group's size. expand_dims now broadcasts a NULL only on rows whose attribute's coordinates include it, for a plain dim as for a group.
  • Removing an entity needs a filter at read. With connection outside partial, a connection attribute's map row names no entity, so the fold's entity anti-join cannot reach it. The read drops a row naming, in an unkeyed group's entity field, an entity the resolved axis no longer holds (since deletion cascades through tombstones, against the group's dead tuples: a label outside the key) — so removing an entity still drops its connections' values.
  • A NULL struct crosses entity types. It expands to every tuple of the group, and connection spans every type, so a constant meant for links reaches buses' connections too. Left open.
  • group_columns stayed, with a smaller meaning: every group but the entity-type group, the coordinates broadcast_dims appends. What went is the derivation of which groups are keyed.
  • set's keywords stage no NULL struct, unlike landing step 3 planned. A missing key coordinate is still refused rather than staged as NULL, as set already did; a NULL struct comes in through a long frame.
  • It grew src/ by 19 lines net rather than shrinking it by 40–80: the read-time filter, the attribute-scoped expansion and the whole-or-NULL check, which reads data where the struct check read only dtypes, cost what the removed derivation saved (what it saves).

docs.title: DEP 11: deletion cascades through tombstones, not through filters
docs.text:
DEP 11 Title deletion cascades through tombstones, not through filters Author Jonas Hörsch Status Implemented 2026-10-13 Requires DEP 10 Created 2026-10-13 Version Unreleased Superseded-By DEP 20 (its removal by tombstone, and dead labels as winning tombstones)

A label is removed by a tombstone, and only by a tombstone: removing one tombstones every group tuple naming it, a layer leaving such a tuple alive is refused, and nothing is inferred on read from a dead label a row refers to.

This supersedes the no-cascade rule the struct proposal kept — "the tuples stand, dangling" — for group tuples; values still never cascade further than the rules below say.

docs.title: What is wrong today
docs.text:
Removing an entity drops the values that name it, but in four places, each covering part of the problem:

Where What it drops Keyed on fold_inputs parent owner-map rows hit by this layer's tombstones: entity, each keyed group, each partial dim owner-key columns, and the entity fields of keyed groups through entity_coordinates _living (read) value rows naming a removed entity in a coordinate outside the owner key the resolved entity axis, through entity_coordinates WorkingRecord._collapsed_inputs staged rows hit by this layer's own entity and tuple tombstones _tombstoned and entity_coordinates resolve_groups only the group's own tombstones –

So after remove("Generator", ["g1"]) the value x(g1, bus0) is gone, but the tuple (g1, bus0) still stands in record.groups["connection"], naming an entity the record no longer has. And the deletion paths go through entity_coordinates and Schema.entity_fields, which hard-code one dim: removing a bus label reaches nothing that names it inside a struct.

docs.title: The rule
docs.text:
1. Removing a label writes the cascade. WorkingRecord.remove(ctype, names) tombstones the entities and every group tuple with a field naming one of them, read from the resolved groups. The folded group then honours its own tombstones, and resolve_groups needs no filter. The API is unchanged; a dim label tombstoned through a layer written directly carries its own cascade, which rule 2 enforces.
  2. write_layer refuses a dangling tuple. A layer that leaves a tuple alive whose field names a label dead after the layer, or adds a tuple naming one, is refused at write time. A layer written by hand carries its own cascade, or fails loudly.
  3. The fold drops keyed values. A coordinate in the owner key — entity, partial dims, partial groups — is anti-joined against the layer's tombstones in fold_inputs, as now. A re-added label starts fresh. The entity anti-join reaches the top-level entity only: a group's entity fields are reached through the group's tuple tombstones rule 1 wrote.
  4. The read drops unkeyed values against dead labels. For a coordinate outside the owner key, ownership is per attribute, so the fold cannot reach the rows. On read, value rows are anti-joined, per such coordinate, against its dead labels: those whose winning row in the fold is a tombstone. For a group that is its dead tuples, one struct column. An equi-join against a set that is usually empty, and skipped when it is.

partial stays what it is — the granularity of an override. It is not transitive: a group drawing on a partial dim need not be partial itself.

docs.title: Dead labels survive materialisation
docs.text:
A materialised node caches the owner map and the folded axes and groups, not value rows, and its folded relations are tombstone-free. So rule 4 cannot take its dead labels from the layers above the base alone:

  • layer 1 sets x(g1, bus0), with connection outside partial;
  • layer 2 removes g1, and so (g1, bus0);
  • layer 3 is materialised;
  • a read at layer 4 takes x's owner from the cached map, layer 1 per attribute, and reads layer 1's file.

Dead labels from above the base alone do not name (g1, bus0), so x(g1, bus0) would come back with nothing re-added. The fold cannot cut them earlier either: along an unkeyed coordinate the owner map holds one row per attribute, not per label, so there is no row for a dead label to remove, only an exception to carry. So the cache keeps them, as dead/<coord>.parquet beside dims/ and groups/, for each dim and group outside partial — a keyed coordinate's dead labels are already cut by the fold — and for each dim a group draws on, which rule 2 checks tuples against below the base too, and rule 4 reads the base's dead labels plus those of the layers above it. The resolved axes and groups stay tombstone-free for every reader that expects them so; fold_axis hands the dead labels back as a by-product of the fold it already does.

A semi-join against the live labels, which the cache already holds, would need no new file, but it runs on every read, where the anti-join against a usually empty set is skipped.

docs.title: Re-adding a label revives its unkeyed values
docs.text:
Layer 1 sets x(g1, bus0); layer 2 removes g1 (and so (g1, bus0)); layer 3 re-adds both. Along a keyed coordinate the fold dropped layer 1's row, so x starts fresh. Along an unkeyed one the owner map still names layer 1 for x, and (g1, bus0) is no longer dead, so x(g1, bus0) comes back — for every unkeyed attribute over the tuple at once.

This is accepted: it is what a coordinate outside partial means — values owned per attribute, not per label. A schema wanting re-adds to start fresh declares the group partial.

docs.title: What it costs
docs.text:
• write_layer depends on the ancestry. "Dead after the layer" needs the parent's resolved axes and groups, so rule 2 is a fold plus one semi-join per group field over the written layer. Today the writer's checks are layer-local but for name uniqueness.
  • Removing a bus removes its connections. A PyPSA component whose bus is removed is left with no connection row, which build reports as a missing bus.
  • The resolved cache grows by a dead-labels file per dim and group outside partial.

docs.title: What goes
docs.text:
• _living, replaced by rule 4's anti-join against dead labels.
  • The entity-field anti-joins through entity_coordinates in fold_inputs and _collapsed_inputs; the top-level entity anti-join stays, as rule 3's keyed case.
  • Every literal entity in the cascade: rules 1–4 are stated over dims and groups.

entity_coordinates and Schema.entity_fields stay for what is not deletion: Fold.flags(ctype) scopes owner-map rows to a type by the entities they name, and set resolves an attribute's entity names (_keyword_entities).

docs.title: To check before building
docs.text: • That nested dims (within) follow rule 1 too: fold_axis keys a nested dim by its axis_key, (period, timestep), so a parent's tombstone does not reach its children today; removing period=2030 would tombstone (2030, t) for every t. Not built: WorkingRecord removes no dim label, and rule 2 checks no tuple field over a nested dim.

docs.title: As built
docs.text:
• Rule 1 is WorkingRecord.remove; a dim label other than an entity is removed only by a layer written directly, which carries its own cascade.
  • Rule 2 runs in write_layer for a layer writing any axis or group, folding the parent's sources and the staged layer. It checks only what the layer does — the tuples it adds, and the tuples still naming a label it removes — so a tuple an ancestor left dangling blocks no later write.
  • Rule 4's anti-join is _living; dead/ holds the coordinates resolve.mortal names.

docs.title: DEP 12: properties — metadata declared apart from data
docs.text:
DEP 12 Title properties — metadata declared apart from data Author Jonas Hörsch Status Implemented 2026-10-13 (steps 1 and 2) Requires DEP 10, DEP 11 Created 2026-10-12 Version Unreleased Replaces DEP 6

Two changes that are one. Properties — what classifies or describes one label of a dim, its metadata — get their own section of the manifest, apart from attributes, the data. And the entity-type axis stops being a dim with a group over entity: it becomes an ordinary Enum property of entity, whose values — categories — per-category defaults and trait scoping key on. With it goes every special case of entity and entity_type in core: entity becomes a dim like any other, listed in partial, and the name entity_type is data a schema happens to declare.

It builds on a group is one struct column — a group is a dim, referenced in rows by one struct column — and on deletion cascading through tombstones.

It lands in two steps. Step 1 — properties, categories, and entity as an ordinary dim — is being built. Step 2 — the section, not the shape, deciding where a value lives — is the rest of the design below, sequenced after. A per-category read, members, is deferred. An optional stage, storing a category in an attribute row, is to be decided.

docs.title: What starts it
docs.text:
Where a value is read depends on how many coordinates address it, not on what it is. p_nom and carrier are both declared under attributes with dims: [entity], so both land on the entity axis — and record.attributes hands over neither, since it holds long frames only; a caller finds them on record.dims["entity"] or record.entity_types["Generator"]. Yet p_nom is data a model optimises against, and carrier a label describing the generator. The rule placing them — exactly one addressing coordinate — groups the two by an accident of shape.

The same rule makes a compatible schema change move a file. Widening p_nom to dims: [entity, scenario] is compatible because NULL broadcasts, but it moves p_nom from a column of the entity axis to inputs/p_nom.parquet, so the rows a layer wrote before are in a file the new schema no longer reads it from.

The entity-type axis is a special case at every layer. It is a dim, plus a group over entity into it, whose rows are the entity axis file rather than a groups/ file — the one exception to a file per group. Its name is reserved as an attribute name. Whether it is declared decides the layout of the entity axis: per-type member files under dims/entity_type/ in one case, columns of dims/entity.parquet in the other. Traits may be scoped by it. Its Enum dtype is what makes it a vocabulary, while a String-typed declaration of it is an open question.

entity is a special case too. It is in the fold key whatever partial says, a NULL in it never broadcasts, its tombstones alone cascade into a group's fields, and the read API answers per entity type (entity_types, entity_type(ctype), flags(ctype)). None of that is said in the schema; all of it is code naming "entity".

And the schema cannot say what a framework's registry says. PyPSA defaults differ per component for one name:

name default per type sign 1 for Generator, Store, StorageUnit; -1 for Load, ShuntImpedance carrier "AC" for Bus; "" otherwise type "primary_energy" for GlobalConstraint; "" otherwise p_min_pu -1 for StorageUnit; 0 otherwise p_set 0 for Load; NaN otherwise

AttributeSpec.default is one value, so today a tool either picks one and writes the others out as data, or loses them. None of the 142 input names differs in dtype between types — only in default.

docs.title: Properties and attributes
docs.text:
dimensions:
  entity: { dtype: String }
  bus: { dtype: String }
  snapshot: { dtype: { Datetime: us } }
  scenario: { dtype: String }

groups:
  connection:
    over: { entity: entity, bus: bus }

properties:
  entity:
    entity_type:
      dtype: { Enum: [Bus, Generator, Load, Link, Store, StorageUnit] }
    carrier:
      dtype: String
      default: ""
      default_by:
        entity_type: { Bus: AC }
    sign:
      dtype: Float64
      default: 1
      default_by:
        entity_type: { Load: -1 }
  bus:
    x: { dtype: Float64, unit: "°" }
    y: { dtype: Float64, unit: "°" }

attributes:
  p_nom:
    dtype: Float64
    dims: [entity]
    default: 0
  p_nom_extendable:
    dtype: Boolean
    dims: [entity]
    default: false
  p_max_pu:
    dtype: Float64
    dims: [entity, snapshot]
    default: 1
  p_min_pu:
    dtype: Float64
    dims: [entity, snapshot]
    default: 0
    default_by:
      entity_type: { StorageUnit: -1 }
  efficiency:
    dtype: Float64
    dims: [connection]
  weight:
    dtype: Float64
    dims: [scenario]
    default: 1

traits:
  generator:
    attributes: [p_max_pu, p_nom_extendable]
    on: { entity_type: [Generator] }
    switch: p_nom_extendable

partial: [entity, scenario, connection]

A property is one value per label of one dim, its subject, and is declared under that subject's key — there is no dims on a property, and it never varies along another axis. It identifies, classifies or describes the label: a type, a carrier, a sign convention, a coordinate on a map.

An attribute is data: what a model reads as part of its problem and what a scenario or a layer would vary. It keeps dims, which may name a single coordinate — p_nom over entity, a scenario weight over scenario — without that making it a property.

Which a name is, is the author's declaration, not derived. The test is the one above, and a tool reads it from its registry where it can.

One name, one spec, across every section. A name declared as a property and as an attribute, or as a property of two subjects, is rejected — flags would have two answers for it. So is a property sharing a dim's or a group's name, which would collide with that coordinate's column. This is the flat-attributes argument extended to the new section.

docs.title: An Enum property of a partial dim categorizes its subject
docs.text:
Any Enum-typed property of a dim listed in partial may be named by Trait.on and default_by. Its values are that dim's categories along it. There is no flag declaring the role, and no limit of one per dim: entity_type categorizes entity, and an Enum-typed carrier would too, as would a bus_type on bus. Naming any other property — a String, or one of a dim outside partial — is refused.

The two conditions are what a category needs:

  • Enum, so the categories a trait or a default names are checkable against a declared vocabulary. This settles the String-typed axis question: a set of categories is an Enum, or nothing can key on it.
  • The dim in partial, because only there is a dim owned and checked per label. Outside it, a layer setting one entity's value would own every entity's, and a label could not be refused against an axis the fold does not key.

That replaces the whole entity-type construct: no entity_type dim, no group over entity into it, no exception to a file per group, and no reserved name — entity_type is a column of dims/entity.parquet because every property of entity is. A schema whose entities have no categories declares no Enum property of entity, and nothing else about it differs. The schema attaches no meaning to the name entity_type; it is what PyPSA and every existing record call it.

Category is the word for such a property's values throughout, because label already names an axis value — what add(dim, labels) and remove(dim, labels) take. Schema.categorizing(dim) lists the properties of dim a trait or default may key on; which attributes a label carries is attributes_for(dim, **categories) — the label's value of each categorizing property — and its default default_for(name, **categories).

A category may change. set("entity_type", "Load", entity="g1") is a patch of one property like any other. The values g1 holds for attributes a Load does not carry stay stored — record.attributes shows what was written — but fall outside every per-category read and every broadcast, which are evaluated against its current categories.

docs.title: default_by — a default per category
docs.text:
default stays the fallback. default_by maps a categorizing property to per-category overrides:

default: 0
default_by:
  entity_type: { StorageUnit: -1 }

A value read unset — a NULL property column, or no inputs/ row reaching the label — reads the first default_by key, in declaration order, whose map lists the label's category; else default.

  • On properties and attributes alike. p_min_pu and p_set need it as much as sign does, and a default is never stored, so it costs no file layout.
  • Each key reachable from the value's address. A key must categorize a dim the value reaches: entity directly, or through connection's entity field for a value over the group. A category outside the property's Enum is refused.
  • Only the default varies. dtype, unit and description are the spec's own and never per category, which is what keeps one name one column and one inputs/ file.

Step 1 declares and validates default_by and answers it through Schema.default_for; applying it on read is step 2.

docs.title: Traits are scoped by a category
docs.text:
Trait.on keeps its shape — on: {entity_type: [Generator, Link]} — and names a categorizing property where it named an entity-type axis; one property per trait, as built. A trait narrows; it does not grant holds unchanged, whichever property each trait keys on: an attribute no trait claims is carried by every label, and a claimed one by every label some claiming trait matches. A trait on entity_type: [Generator] and one on carrier: [wind], both claiming p_max_pu, give it to every generator and every wind entity. Every trait in the PyPSA tool reads as before.

A switch is addressed by exactly the dim its trait's property categorizes, and a trait with a switch must have an on.

switch is not subsumed. A category is a property — one value per label, never varying along another axis — while a switch may: p_nom_extendable per investment_period is a trait an entity carries in some periods and not others. Lifting the trait-switches restriction to the categorized dim exactly is step 2: switch would then name a property of the subject or an attribute addressed by it and further dims. Which categories may carry a value stays a schema answer; which labels do in a given period stays a question about data.

docs.title: A NULL reaches the labels carrying the attribute
docs.text: entity broadcasts like any dim: a row leaving it NULL means every entity. On a categorized dim, every is narrowed by the schema — a NULL expands only to the labels that carry the attribute (attributes_for), judged by their categories at read time. set("p_max_pu", 0.9) reaches every generator, those added in a later layer included, and never a bus. One filter where the fold expands a NULL, and the old "every entity whose type declares it" without a list of names stored.

docs.title: entity is an ordinary dim
docs.text:
With the categories a property and the fold key a schema declaration, nothing in core names entity:

  • The fold key is exactly what partial lists — dims and groups alike. Every dim and every group broadcasts. A dim a group draws on need not be in partial: its dead labels are kept and dropped on read (deletion).
  • Deletion is tombstones cascading: remove(dim, labels) tombstones the labels and every live tuple of a group with a field over dim naming one; the fold anti-joins the tombstones of every partial dim and group.
  • The read API answers per record, not per type: Record, Resolver, Fold and LayerData lose entity_types, entity_type(ctype) and entity_axis, and flags() takes no type. A per-category frame is dims[dim] filtered on a categorizing column.
  • Uniqueness across types is structural: one axis row per label.

docs.title: One file per subject on disk
docs.text:
On disk, every property of a dim is a column of dims/<dim>.parquet, categories and all, NULL on a row whose category does not carry it. dims/entity_type/<Type>.parquet goes, and with it the second entity-axis layout the member-file proposal introduced: a record with and one without categories have one layout, differing by one column.

Per-type files existed because every type has a different column set. The schema now says which columns each category carries, so a category's frame is a filter on its property and a projection to those columns — recoverable from one file, where per-type files would state each entity's category twice, once in the column and once in the filename. Parquet stores an all-NULL column chunk for almost nothing and DuckDB reads only what it projects. Only a per-category dtype would need per-category files, and that is ruled out above.

docs.title: Editing is generic over dims
docs.text:
WorkingRecord loses its per-type calls (add(ctype, frame), remove(ctype, names), set(..., entity=…)) for ones over any dim:

w.add("entity", ["g1", "g2"], entity_type="Generator", carrier="wind")
w.set("carrier", "solar", entity="g2")  # a property: one column of one axis row
w.set("p_max_pu", 0.9)  # every generator, now and later
w.set("efficiency", 0.7, entity="l1", bus="b0")  # a group's fields by keyword
w.set(
    "p_max_pu", 0.8, entity_type="Generator", carrier="wind"
)  # the wind generators there are now
w.remove("entity", ["g1"])  # tombstones g1 and its connections
  • add(dim, labels, **columns) writes whole axis rows: a column must be one the axis file has — a property, a single-dim attribute, a parent key of a nested dim. An Enum property's value must be one of its categories.
  • set(attribute, value, **coords) addresses every coordinate by keyword, a group's fields included. It writes a property too, a category included, as a patch of one column of the axis row.
  • A property keyword selects labels when set is called. entity_type="Generator", carrier="wind" resolves to the labels matching both on the record as staged, and set writes one row per label — nothing of the filter is stored. A label added later is not reached; a plain NULL (every label carrying the attribute) and default_by are the two ways a value reaches labels not yet added. Storing a category in the row instead is the optional stage.
  • remove(dim, labels) writes axis tombstones and cascades to group tuples.

Adding a component with its connections and varying values is now add, add_group and a set per attribute, where the old wide-frame add split one frame three ways. Whether a wide-frame convenience comes back, over the generic calls, is open below.

docs.title: Step 2: the section decides where a value lives
docs.text:
declared as lands in property of a dim dims/<dim>.parquet — a column of the axis file attribute, any dims inputs/<attr>.parquet — long rows

That replaces where a value lives as a rule over len(dims). inputs/p_nom.parquet is entity | attribute | breakpoint | value, one row per entity, and widening p_nom over scenario adds a column to the same file — NULL in every row written before, which is what the broadcast rule needs to read them unchanged. An axis file then carries only its labels, its within keys, its tombstones and the subject's properties; no data.

Step 1 keeps single-dim attributes as axis columns, so no file moves yet.

In the API each accessor then holds one section:

record.dims["entity"]  # entity — labels only
record.properties["entity"]  # entity | entity_type | carrier | sign | ...
record.attributes["p_nom"]  # entity | attribute | breakpoint | value
record.attributes["p_max_pu"]  # entity | snapshot | attribute | breakpoint | value

properties[dim] holds stored values, no defaults applied. A framework's static frame — PyPSA's n.generators — is that frame filtered on a category, its default_by filled, and joined with the entity-only rows of its attributes; the tool keeps calling it entity_types. Schema.attributes_for splits into properties_for and attributes_for, both narrowed by the same traits.

Also step 2: properties of a group (connection.role, today an attribute over connection), and per-category flags — flags() per record loses what PyPSA's verify checked per type.

docs.title: Optional: members
docs.text:
Status: deferred — not part of the accepted scope, until a caller needs it. properties[dim], stored values without defaults, and flags(**categories) cover what is read today.

record.members(
    "entity", entity_type="Generator"
)  # entity | carrier | sign | ... — its rows, its properties

A per-category read — members here, the name open — would filter a dim's labels on its categorizing properties and project to the properties those labels carry, with default_by applied; no attribute columns. A framework's static frame would be that frame joined with the entity-only rows of its attributes.

docs.title: Optional stage: categories in attribute rows
docs.text:
Status: to be decided — implications first, independent of step 2.

A row of inputs/ would carry a categorizing property as a column, narrowing a NULL along its dim: entity NULL and entity_type = Generator reads "every generator", those added in a later layer included, where a staging-time filter writes the generators there are now.

inputs/p_max_pu.parquet
entity | entity_type | snapshot | attribute | breakpoint | value
NULL   | Generator   | NULL     | p_max_pu  | NULL       | 0.9    every generator, now and later
g7     | NULL        | NULL     | p_max_pu  | NULL       | 0.5    one label

It is the step-1 broadcast filter — a NULL reaching only the labels carrying the attribute — with a category chosen by the row as well as by the schema.

What it would mean:

  • The format. Every attribute reaching a categorized dim gains its categorizing properties as columns of its long rows — long_columns_for grows by one per property reached. Adding one to a schema is compatible: old rows read NULL, which filters nothing.
  • Reach follows the category. The filter is evaluated at read time against each label's current category, so a label re-categorized by set moves into or out of the row's reach — what "every wind generator" means. A non-Enum property cannot be stored as a filter, as it cannot key a trait.
  • The fold. The filter applies where a NULL is expanded, against the resolved axis, before the owner map is keyed, so the owner key keeps its shape and the column never reaches a reader. A row naming its label explicitly has the column NULL; a non-NULL category on an explicit label is redundant at best and is refused.
  • Overlap within one layer. Today a staged row is replaced by its key. A category row and an explicit row, or two category rows on different properties, have different keys and reach the same label. That needs a specificity rule — explicit label over category row over plain NULL — and two rows of equal specificity reaching one label refused at staging.
  • Overlap across layers is unchanged: last writer wins per expanded key, so a later layer's category row overrides an earlier layer's explicit value for every label it reaches, exactly as a later plain NULL does.
  • Flags. broadcast says a row left a dim NULL; a category row is a narrowed broadcast. Either it counts as broadcast (the narrowing invisible to flags) or flags gains a third state.
  • Groups. A value over connection reaches entity through a field; its category column names the category of that field. A group drawing twice on one categorized dim — a corridor (from, to) — would need a column per field, and is refused until wanted.
  • Against default_by. Two per-category mechanisms: the schema's default and a layer's category row. Data wins where it reaches; the default fills the rest. The difference is who declares it — a schema author once, or any layer.
  • The read and the write. record.attributes stays per label, the category expanded away; write_layer checks the column's values are categories carrying the attribute; set(..., entity_type=…) writes the column instead of resolving labels.

What would decide it: a case where layer data, not the schema, must reach every label of one category, those not yet added included, for an attribute other categories carry too. Until one appears, staging-time filters cover the rest.

docs.title: What this buys
docs.text:
The entity-type special cases go. The dim, the group into it, the group-file exception, the reserved name, the two entity-axis layouts, and every literal "entity" in core — all of them were there to make one dim and one of its properties special.

Categories need no new construct. An Enum property of a partial dim is one; any dim may have several, and a bus_type scopes traits and defaults over buses exactly as entity_type does over entities.

A registry's per-type defaults round-trip. sign, carrier, p_min_pu and p_set are declared as PyPSA defines them instead of written out as data or lost.

Step 2: each section answers where its values are read, p_nom included — the confusion this starts from — and widening an attribute's dims is compatible in fact.

docs.title: What it costs
docs.text:
The read API answers less, for now. No per-type flags until step 2, no per-type frame and no applied defaults; PyPSA filters the entity axis itself, and its verify counts an attribute one type owns as owned by every type.

partial must list what used to be implicit. A schema keying traits or defaults on entity's categories must put entity in partial; a schema omitting it is refused rather than silently keyed.

A category is schema vocabulary. Making carrier categorizing means an Enum, so adding a carrier is a schema change.

Re-categorized labels keep stale values. A label whose category changes keeps what it held for attributes it no longer carries; they are out of every per-category read's reach, but stored.

Entity-only data reads through the fold, not the axis (step 2). p_nom was a column resolved with the entity row; it becomes long rows keyed by the fold key like any attribute — a static frame of forty columns is forty attribute reads and a pivot where it was one file.

The choice is the author's, and can be wrong. Nothing derives whether x on a bus is metadata or data; a schema declaring it either way is valid. Moving a name between sections moves its file and is an incompatible change.

A per-type value addressed by the type alone loses its home. An icon per entity type lived on dims/entity_type.parquet; with no entity_type dim there is no file keyed by category. Nothing in the tools declares one; if a case appears, it is a property of a dim declared for the purpose.

Every manifest is rewritten, and every record re-exported: the entity-type dim and group become one property, and entity joins partial. Breaking changes are free.

docs.title: What it opens
docs.text:
Whether a functional group over one coordinate is a property. country over [bus] into country is one label per bus — metadata, of a dtype ranging over a dim. The old entity-type axis was exactly that, and this proposal turns it into a property; into might go the same way, or the chain argument might keep it a group.

Whether wide-frame editing comes back — one call adding a component with its properties, connections and values, built on add, add_group and set, as the inverse of what to_datarecord produces.

Whether a broadcast survives materialisation. A materialised ancestor's owner map stores a NULL row already expanded to the labels that existed then, and seeds a child's fold without re-expanding. So set("p_max_pu", 0.9) reaches a generator added — or re-categorized — in a child only while the ancestor is unmaterialised; plain NULLs behave the same today. One level down, a WorkingRecord folds its committed prefix once, so a label staged or re-categorized there is not reached by a parent's NULL even while the parent is unmaterialised. To be gone into once this proposal is built.

Whether groups edit like dims. A group is a dim, yet is edited through add_group/remove_group with a struct frame where set takes its fields by keyword; add(name, keys, **columns) over a group would close that.

docs.title: Status
docs.text:
Steps 1 and 2 are built on feat/properties-structs, and the design pages, usage pages and changelog follow them. Two departures from the text above:

  • No partial rule for groups. A dim a group draws on need not be in partial; its dead labels already cover deletion. The only partial requirement is a categorized dim's.
  • A default_by is applied by its reader. record.properties and record.attributes show stored rows, and a reader fills a per-category default through Schema.default_for, as the PyPSA tool does.

Neither members nor the optional stage is built.

docs.title: How to know it worked
docs.text:
No entity or entity_type in src/datarecord outside tools/, docstrings and tests. The names are only data — a dim and a property a schema happens to declare.

A record with and one without categories differ on disk by one column. Same files, dims/entity.parquet with or without entity_type, no dims/entity_type/ in either.

A category on bus works like one on entity. A trait on: {bus_type: [DC]} narrows attributes over bus, and default_by: {bus_type: …} validates.

Two categorizing properties of one dim combine. Traits on entity_type: [Generator] and carrier: [wind] claiming one attribute give it to both sets of labels.

set("p_max_pu", 0.9) reaches every generator, a later-added one included, and no bus.

A trait keyed on a String property, or on a property of a dim outside partial, is refused.

PyPSA round-trips sign and p_min_pu with nothing written (step 2). An add of a Load and a StorageUnit setting neither reads back sign == -1 and p_min_pu == -1.

p_nom is in record.attributes (step 2), inputs/p_nom.parquet holds one row per entity, and widening it over scenario reads an old layer's values back in every scenario.

docs.title: DEP 13: Buses and carriers are dims
DEP 13: buses and carriers are dims
docs.text:
DEP 13 Title buses and carriers are dims Author Jonas Hoersch, Bryn Pickering Status Implemented 2026-10-15 Requires DEP 12 Created 2026-10-14 Version Unreleased

Once implemented, the tool page, the schema and the format are authoritative where they and this text disagree.

docs.title: Abstract
docs.text: In the PyPSA tool, Bus and Carrier stop being entity types: a bus is a label of the bus dim, a carrier a label of a new carrier dim, and what PyPSA stores on either is a property of the label or an attribute over the dim. Two core changes carry it: a property may be into a dim — its values are that dim's labels — and a property's name is scoped to its subject and addressed as subject.name.

docs.title: Motivation
docs.text: A bus exists twice: as a label of bus, which connection ranges over, and as an entity of type Bus holding v_nom, x, carrier; nothing joins the two but the spelling, so remove on either leaves half. Because the bus is an entity, a Bus and a Load both named north — every clustered pypsa-eur network — is a collision, Bus.x and Line.x are one attribute, and Bus.p cannot be written. A carrier is a string no axis checks. PyPSA#1474 makes buses and carriers indices, the same way.

docs.title: The schema PyPSA declares
docs.text:
dimensions:
  entity: { dtype: String }
  bus: { dtype: String }
  carrier: { dtype: String }
  snapshot: { dtype: { Datetime: us } }
  scenario: { dtype: String }

groups:
  connection: { over: { entity: entity, bus: bus } }

properties:
  entity:
    component: # was `entity_type`; PyPSA's word for Generator, Line, ...
      dtype: { Enum: [Generator, Line, Link, Load, Process, ShuntImpedance, StorageUnit, Store, SubNetwork, Transformer] }
    carrier: { into: carrier }
    sign: { dtype: Float64, default: 1, default_by: { entity.component: { Load: -1 } } }
    type: { dtype: String, default: "" } # PyPSA's standard type, unrenamed
  bus:
    carrier: { into: carrier, default: AC }
    type: { dtype: String, default: "" }
    x: { dtype: Float64, default: 0 }
    y: { dtype: Float64, default: 0 }
    unit: { dtype: String, default: "" }
    location: { dtype: String, default: "" }
  carrier:
    color: { dtype: String, default: "" }
    nice_name: { dtype: String, default: "" }
  connection:
    role: { dtype: { Enum: [input, output, attached] } }

attributes:
  x: { dtype: Float64, dims: [entity], default: 0 } # a Line's reactance
  v_nom: { dtype: Float64, dims: [bus], default: 1 }
  v_mag_pu_set: { dtype: Float64, dims: [bus, snapshot, scenario], default: 1 }
  co2_emissions: { dtype: Float64, dims: [carrier], default: 0 }
  # ... every other registry input as today

results:
  marginal_price: { dtype: Float64, dims: [bus, snapshot, scenario] }
  # ...

partial: [entity, bus, scenario, connection]

docs.title: The tool
docs.text:
• entity.component, renamed from entity_type, categorizes entity; its Enum is the types exported as entities — no Bus, no Carrier. Shape and GlobalConstraint are out of scope, as today. on and default_by name a categorizing property dotted.
  • Placement follows the properties rule, read off the registry per name; every name is PyPSA's.
PyPSA record Bus.type, Bus.carrier, Bus.x, Bus.y, Bus.unit, Bus.location properties of bus Bus.v_nom, Bus.v_mag_pu_min, Bus.v_mag_pu_max, Bus.v_mag_pu_set attributes over bus (and the varying dims) Bus.marginal_price, Bus.v_mag_pu, Bus.v_ang results over bus and the varying dims Bus.p, Bus.q, Bus.control, Bus.generator, Bus.sub_network not written: derived from the connections a custom Bus or Carrier column attribute over its dim, as a custom entity column is Carrier.color, Carrier.nice_name properties of carrier Carrier.co2_emissions, max_growth, max_relative_growth attributes over carrier a component's carrier entity.carrier, into carrier
  • partial gains bus, not carrier: a layer patches one bus's v_nom; it restates every carrier's co2_emissions, a few dozen rows.
  • Deletion. remove("bus", …) is the cascade every dim has; an entity left unattached is verify's to report. remove("carrier", …) is refused while a stored carrier names the label, as a label a tuple still names is.
  • Collisions are within a dim. A bus and a load may share a name; two exported types may not.
  • A custom column clashes only with an attribute: custom Bus.country beside custom Generator.country is country with two dims, reported via Requirements.columns as today; a name a property has does not clash.
  • to_datarecord writes the two axes in PyPSA's order, adds every carrier named but not listed in n.carriers, and stores "" as NULL. build rebuilds n.buses and n.carriers from axis, properties with defaults and attribute rows, series by flags, bus results from outputs.

docs.title: A property into a dim
docs.text: PropertySpec.into names a declared dim; the property's values are its labels and its dtype is the dim's. A stored value must name a live label, checked where a group field is — set, add, the writer; NULL means none. It does not categorize: a category is a schema Enum, labels are data. Any subject may declare one. A group over one coordinate into a dim is refused; into on a group stays for two or more coordinates, and a chain is still not denormalised.

docs.title: A property's name is its subject's
docs.text:
One name, one spec holds for attributes and results. A property is a column of its subject's file, and its name is unique there only: x on bus beside the attribute x, carrier on entity, on bus and as a dim, type on both, Shape's attribute component beside entity.component. Refused at schema load:

  • a property named like its subject's key — the dim, a within parent, or a group's struct column;
  • a property of a group named like one of its coordinates, which are the keywords a tuple is addressed by;
  • two spellings differing only in case, record-wide, and a . in any name (names).

A property is always addressed as subject.name — bus.carrier, connection.role, entity.component. A plain name is an attribute or result, or unknown, the error suggesting the dotted forms of properties so named. Resolution reads the name alone, never the keywords. Schema.resolve(name) returns the AttributeSpec or (subject, PropertySpec) and is what set, default_for, flags and staging call; subject_of and property_spec(name) go. A trait bundles a property by its dotted name.

A selector keyword is bare and names a coordinate of the attribute or a categorizing property of a dim it reaches, coordinate first: carrier="gas" on co2_emissions is the dim; component="Generator" on p_max_pu is entity.component, never the Shape attribute. add(dim, labels, **columns) takes the dim's properties bare. kind="outputs" and an nw.Expr refuse a dotted name. flags and the frames of properties[subject] keep plain names.

docs.title: Pages that change
docs.text:
• tools → collision example Generator/Load; partial sentence; properties list; the table above; the five derived bus results; custom-column clash narrowed.
  • format → collision example; where a value lives loses "no column on the classified axis"; "one name, one spec" scoped to attributes.
  • schema → into on a property, per-subject rule, dotted addressing, the example; into one-coordinate rule; names; partial "not timestep or carrier".
  • record → "never a load"; flags plain names.
  • working record → dotted set, selector rule; validation unknown-name error; add / remove referenced-label refusal.
  • usage schema, reading, editing, CHANGELOG.md; entity_type → component in the tool, the pages and ~20 test files (core: two docstrings).

docs.title: Rationale
docs.text:
x and y are properties, v_nom an attribute, by the rule and not by dtype: a coordinate describes a bus as sign describes a load, and the schema page's own metadata example is bus: {x: …}; v_nom is the per-unit base the model reads and a reinforcement layer changes.

The record-wide name rule protects a file, and a property has one. It exists so inputs/x.parquet is one file with one value dtype; a property's file is its subject's, so what remains to protect is a column in that file and the keywords addressing it. A prefix (bus_x) would spell the subject into the name a second time; the dot spells it once.

into on a property is the smallest reference. It reuses the word and the live-label check a group field already has, settles the single-coordinate into question by removing the group form, and sharing the dim's name lets the column join the axis on itself.

Costs. Every PyPSA record stops reading (component's Enum and name, names moving section, bus rows re-keyed) and is re-exported, breaking changes being free. Every property set in the tool, pages and tests becomes dotted. The fold key widens by one. A round trip may add carrier rows and reads a listed "" carrier as none. Removing a referenced carrier is two edits. A one-coordinate into group is refused.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
record.dims["carrier"]  # carrier
record.properties["bus"]  # bus | carrier | type | x | y | unit | location
record.properties["entity"]  # entity | component | carrier | sign | type
record.attributes["v_nom"]  # bus | attribute | breakpoint | value
record.outputs["marginal_price"]  # bus | snapshot | scenario | ...

w.add("carrier", ["H2"], color="#f0f")
w.add("bus", ["north H2"], carrier="H2", x=10.1, y=52.0)  # bare: the dim's own
w.set("v_nom", 380.0, bus="north")
w.set("bus.x", 10.2, bus="north")  # `x` alone is a Line's reactance
w.set("entity.component", "Load", entity="g1")
w.set("entity.carrier", "coal", entity="g1")  # refused: no label `coal`
w.set("carrier", "AC")  # unknown; did you mean `bus.carrier` or `entity.carrier`
w.set("p_max_pu", 0.8, component="Generator")  # selector: the category
w.remove("bus", ["south"])  # and every connection at it
w.remove("carrier", ["gas"])  # refused while a carrier names it

docs.title: Implementation notes
docs.text:
1. Core: _check_names per-subject refusals; Schema.resolve; dotted set, default_for, flags, staging; . already refused.
  2. Core: PropertySpec.into — parse, live-label check in set/add/writer, remove refusal, one-coordinate into group refused.
  3. Tool: _AXIS_TYPES = {Bus: bus, Carrier: carrier} out of the entity loop; carrier dim; BUS_PROPERTIES/CARRIER_PROPERTIES; _DERIVED_RESULTS["Bus"]; partial; entity_type → component.
  4. Tool: _NetworkSource writes the axes, properties and bus/carrier-keyed rows; missing carriers; clash check narrowed; Bus out of the name-collision check.
  5. Tool: build from axes, properties, attributes and outputs; verify reports an unattached entity.
  6. Pages, usage, changelog, tests dotted and renamed; fixtures re-exported.

Checks: no entity_type outside the proposals; a Bus and a Generator named north round-trip; n.buses/n.carriers round-trip under PyPSA's names; marginal_price keyed by bus; x and bus.x reach their own, set("carrier", "AC") names both dotted forms; remove("carrier", …) refused while referenced; verify reports Bus.country beside Generator.country and passes Generator.location beside bus.location.

docs.title: Rejected Ideas
docs.text:
• Carrier as into groups (entity_carrier, bus_carrier): two files stating what one column of the label's row says.
  • carrier as an unchecked String: no reference, "" and NULL both none, removal dangles.
  • Prefixing bus columns — a written table (bus_x, bus_type), a registry rule (gives bus_x beside y), or every column: a namespace spelled into the name when the subject already is one.
  • Resolving a plain name by the keywords it comes with, or falling back to a uniquely declared property: a name's meaning must not depend on the call's other arguments, nor change when another subject later declares it.
  • Scoping attributes per dim too: an attribute is one file and one place in the fold key.
  • Renaming PyPSA's type to std_type so the category could be type: keeps PyPSA's names only where convenient.
  • carrier in partial, writing Bus.p/q (p is one spec over connection), bus.type as an Enum (free text in PyPSA).

docs.title: Open Issues
docs.text:
• Whether a property into a partial dim may categorize it — a vocabulary that is data, keyed as entity.carrier.
  • Whether a default (bus.carrier: AC) must name a live label; a default is never stored or checked.
  • Whether bus earns its fold-key column, measured on a pypsa-eur-sized record.
  • Whether a custom bus column can be a property, which would dissolve the one remaining custom-column clash.
  • Whether selector keywords need a qualified form, for a categorizing name on two dims one attribute reaches.
  • What PyPSA#1474 lands as: an unlisted carrier may become an error, "" may stop meaning none.

docs.title: DEP 14: Combining a record with an extension
DEP 14: combining a record with an extension
docs.text: DEP 14 Title combining a record with an extension Author Jonas Hörsch, Bryn Pickering Status Rejected 2026-10-20 Requires DEP 12, DEP 13 Created 2026-10-14

docs.title: Abstract
docs.text: combine(base, extension, con) presents a tool's record and the data a consumer derives beside it as one lazy RecordLike under one united schema, to read directly or write as one record. The extension adds names and never redefines one. The idea and its first prototype are Bryn Pickering's (PR #56); this redesigns it against the current RecordLike.

docs.title: Motivation
docs.text:
A PyPSA-Eur workflow exports its network with PyPSA.to_datarecord(n, ws.con), under the tool's schema. Beside it, the workflow holds data PyPSA does not model, keyed by the same entities, buses and periods: custom constraints, a country per bus, an emission intensity per generator. There is no correct way to put both in one record:

  • A layer declares nothing. There is one schema per record, so w.set("co2_intensity", …) is refused as undeclared.
  • A hand-written union is unchecked. A child layer under a wider schema widens the manifest, but the check is compatibility, which lets the union change a base attribute's default or unit or widen a base Enum.
  • A property on a shared subject cannot be added by a layer. An axis row wins whole per label (one fold for every axis), so a child adding bus.country must restate every base property of each bus.
  • A standalone directory is one source with one schema.

docs.title: Uniting the schemas
docs.text:
base.schema.extended_by(extension.schema) -> Schema returns the united schema or raises ValueError naming the entry and the rule:

entry the extension may add a shared one must refused dim a new dim, within any dim be identical a differing re-declaration group a new group, over and into any dims be identical a differing re-declaration property subject.name a new name, on a new or a shared subject be identical a differing re-declaration attribute, result a new name, over any dims and groups be identical a differing re-declaration trait a new trait, on any categorizing property be identical attributes or switch naming anything the base declares partial its new dims and groups — a shared dim or group the base's partial lacks meta key a new key hold an equal value a differing value

Identical is equal as declared, unit, default and default_by included. Re-declaring is how an extension's schema stays valid alone: a trait on entity.component needs the entity dim, the entity.component property and entity in partial declared. version is the base's and not compared. The united schema then passes Schema's own validator.

Invariant: every base name keeps its spec and every base category carries what it did, so extended_by(...).compatible_with(base) is always empty.

docs.title: The combined record
docs.text:
combine computes the united schema and refuses an extension holding rows of an attribute or result the base declares, both at the call and from the mapping keys alone (Frames). Every frame is planned on con through as_relation, so a relation from another connection is refused and nothing is collected.

  • dims, groups: union by key, the base's keys in its order, then the extension's new keys in its order (axis order).
  • properties[s]: joined per subject over the united keys. A base-declared column comes from the base for its keys and from the extension for keys only the extension holds; an extension-added column comes from the extension; anything else reads NULL.
  • attributes, outputs: by name, each one side's frame unchanged.
  • flags(**categories): computed from the combined frames against the united schema, by the protocol's definition.

combine is a read-time view. It folds nothing and removes nothing, takes any RecordLike on either side (a tool's record, a Record, a WorkingRecord, another combination), and becomes an ordinary record when written: ws.write(combine(...), uri), store.root(...), or rev.child(combine(rev.record, ext, con)), whose manifest widening the invariant guarantees. It is not a Record, so it is edited after being written.

FrameRecord(schema, dims=, properties=, groups=, attributes=, outputs=) is an extension's shape: native frames of any backend narwhals reads. A subject with properties and no dims frame takes its labels from the properties' key, and a declared column a frame lacks reads NULL.

combine and FrameRecord live in core as datarecord/combine.py, and extended_by in schema.py beside compatible_with (module layout).

docs.title: Rationale
docs.text:
The rule protects the base, not only its names. A new trait claiming p_nom for generators collides with nothing yet takes it from every other entity, because a trait narrows. Identity on shared entries plus new traits claiming only new names is what makes the invariant hold, so a tool reads a combined record's base names as it reads its own record.

Subjects split by key, attributes by name. An axis or group row is keyed by one label, so the two sides meet on it. Attribute rows overlap through broadcast, and dividing them between sources is the fold, which is a layer's job. For the same reason, an extension's value for a base-declared column on a base-held key is not read: changing a base value is a layer's job.

What it costs. flags is a scan per call where a Record's is free. An extension may add labels to a shared axis, so a mistyped label becomes a new one. An extension disagreeing with the base on a base-held key goes unnoticed. Re-declaring shared entries makes an extension verbose.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
base = PyPSA.to_datarecord(n, ws.con)
s = base.schema
schema = Schema(
    dimensions={
        "entity": s.dimensions["entity"],
        "bus": s.dimensions["bus"],
        "period": s.dimensions["period"],
        "limit": Dimension(dtype=nw.String()),
    },
    properties={
        "entity": {"component": s.properties["entity"]["component"]},
        "bus": {"country": PropertySpec(dtype=nw.String())},
    },
    attributes={
        "limit_constant": AttributeSpec(dtype=nw.Float64(), dims={"limit", "period"}),
        "co2_intensity": AttributeSpec(dtype=nw.Float64(), dims={"entity"}),
    },
    traits={
        "emitting": Trait(
            attributes={"co2_intensity"}, on={"entity.component": {"Generator", "Link"}}
        )
    },
    partial={"entity"},
)
extension = FrameRecord(
    schema,
    properties={"bus": countries},  # bus | country
    attributes={"limit_constant": limits, "co2_intensity": intensities},
)
record = combine(base, extension, ws.con)
record.flags(component="Generator")["co2_intensity"]
ws.write(record, "resources/networks/base_s_37.record")

docs.title: Implementation notes
docs.text:
1. Schema.extended_by, a parametrized test per refused row, and a test that compatible_with(base) is empty.
  2. combine's members over con, ordered by numbering each side's rows and sorting outermost.
  3. The frames-based flags, sharing categorized_dim, selected and attributes_among with the fold's.
  4. FrameRecord, exported with combine from datarecord.
  5. Pages: a "Combining records" section on writing, extended_by under one schema per record, module layout, usage, changelog.

Checks: reading every member of a combination over frames that raise on collect runs no query; projected to base names and keys, every combined frame equals the base's; flags(component="Bus") lacks co2_intensity.

docs.title: Rejected Ideas
docs.text:
• An extension layer, whether declaring its own schema additions or written under a hand-united schema. The first is the layered schema one schema per record rejects. Both need a tree, cannot be read before written, and restate the base's properties of every shared subject.
  • The prototype's eager widening, which collected both sides to pyarrow and broke lazy Frames.
  • Refusing only colliding trait names, which lets a new trait narrow base attributes.
  • Taking flags from the sides. The extension has no category data, and the PyPSA tool's record answers {}.
  • Merging two sides' rows of one attribute. Dividing overlapping rows is a fold.

docs.title: Open Issues
docs.text:
• Data checks on shared subjects. Should extension-only labels on a shared axis, or disagreement on a base-held key, be refused? Either check needs both frames read, perhaps by the writer.
  • Relaxing identity. Should the extension be allowed to widen a base Enum, or add a trait without on that bundles base names?
  • Adding an extension to an existing tree without restating the base. This needs axis rows folded per column.

docs.title: DEP 15: a dim is flat
docs.text: DEP 15 Title a dim is flat Author Jonas Hoersch Status Implemented (2026-10-20) Requires DEP 13 Created 2026-10-19 Version Unreleased

docs.title: Abstract
docs.text: Dimension.within leaves core: every dim is one label set, keyed by its label alone. A label that today names a point only inside a parent becomes a label unique across its dim plus a property into the parent — snapshot.period into period — the reference DEP 13 added. A chain is a chain of such properties; several parents are several.

docs.title: Motivation
docs.text:
A multi-period PyPSA network declares snapshot within period, and every place that touches the snapshot axis pays for it:

  • Every series carries its period. Every input and result over snapshot is over period too, so p_max_pu is keyed by (entity, period, snapshot), and a NULL period is a second way of reaching a snapshot (tools).
  • Checks skip a nested dim. A property into one, or a group field over one, is not checked by remove or the writer; remove does not cascade to its tuples; the trait check passes over a nested partial dim; set("dim.name", mapping) refuses one. The page lists the first as an open question.
  • Known bugs. An attribute over a nested dim is accepted without its parent, so its rows name no point. A pointwise set with a NULL period drops the rest of the series.
  • The consumer has no nested dims. math-spec, the model-spec language datarecord feeds, gives every dimension one list of members. A multi-period snapshot there is one flat dim with a snapshot → period relation, and its guidance reads: two dimensions that depend on each other, declared as a product cut back by a mask, are one relation. A tool feeding it flattens the (period, snapshot) key anyway.

docs.title: One key column
docs.text:
Dimension is dtype, unit and description. A dim's key is its label: dims/<dim>.parquet is keyed by the one column <dim>, record.dims[dim] is that column, and its labels are unique across the dim. A manifest declaring within is refused at load, the error naming the property into the parent that replaces it.

A label scoped per parent is a flat label and a property into the parent. The source picks the labels; they need only be unique across the dim. What the source called the point inside its parent, if it matters, is a further property.

declared today declared under this DEP timestep within period snapshot; snapshot.period into period; snapshot.timestep timestep in period in horizon snapshot.period into period; period.horizon into horizon timestep within {period, stage} snapshot.period into period; snapshot.stage into stage

A chain is not denormalised, as for any classification: snapshot carries no horizon column, the horizon being a join through period.

Selecting by a parent is a selector keyword. One is bare and matches any property of a dim the attribute reaches (set), so period=2030 on p_max_pu picks the snapshots whose snapshot.period is 2030, and timestep=t0 the snapshot at t0 in every period. Two reached dims both declaring period stay refused.

docs.title: What loses its special case
docs.text: where today, for a nested dim under this DEP axis key, record.dims[dim] (*parents, dim), Schema.axis_key dim axis fold, dead labels keyed by the parents too by the label broadcast a series carries its parent; a NULL parent reaches every period a NULL dim reaches every label add(dim, …) parent keys required properties only set("dim.name", mapping) refused as on any dim remove, the writer no into check, no group cascade, no field check every dim label and trait check on set skipped for a partial dim every partial dim property names none named like a within parent snapshot.period allowed versioning changing within incompatible entry goes

docs.title: The PyPSA tool
docs.text:
• A single-period network's schema is unchanged.
  • A multi-period network's snapshot is flat: its label is PyPSA's timestep where the timesteps are unique across periods, an integer position otherwise. snapshot.period is into period; snapshot.timestep is declared only beside positions, a timestep label holding it already.
  • Inputs and results over snapshot are no longer over period; period_weighting_objective and _years stay over period.
  • build rebuilds the snapshot MultiIndex in axis order from snapshot.period and the label or snapshot.timestep.

docs.title: Pages that change
docs.text:
• schema → Dimension without within; dimensions "its type"; within replaced by a short "a dim is flat" with the table above; within is not into's chain and cross-level paragraphs move to properties; properties loses the within-parent refusal; versioning loses its entry.
  • record → dims[dim] and the axis row without within keys.
  • format → an axis file carries its key, tombstones and properties.
  • layers and working record → the nested-dim exemptions; validation loses the missing parent key.
  • tools → the multi-period paragraph as above.
  • open questions → the into-over-a-nested-dim entry goes; "whether within should subsume bus" goes.
  • usage schema, reading, editing, CHANGELOG.md.

docs.title: Rationale
docs.text:
The scoping belongs to the source's labels, not to the axis. t1 names nothing alone because PyPSA reuses it per period, and a source that numbers its snapshots once has no nesting to declare. Moving the scoping into a property states the same relation in the one form the record already checks, folds and selects on, and a consumer reads snapshot.period exactly as it reads bus.carrier.

One key column is one rule. The axis key, the fold key and the broadcast rule each had a branch for (*parents, dim), and every check that could not place a label by one column skipped it rather than branch. Removing the shape removes the skips: the bugs above are not fixed, they become unrepresentable — no attribute can be over a nested dim without its parent when no dim has a parent, and no series carries a parent to leave NULL.

into can now express timestep. The distinction held because within scoped a label set and into could not. A flat label set makes the snapshot a classification like any other: each snapshot picks one period.

The NULL-parent set bug is narrower than within. It is a fold bug with any two whole-owned dims, which within made routine by putting a second whole-owned dim on every series. It goes from the snapshot and stays for other schemas.

Costs. A source whose inner labels repeat across parents must synthesise unique ones. Every record declaring within stops reading and is re-exported, breaking changes being free. "The same timestep in every period" is no longer one row with a NULL period but a selector over snapshot.timestep, which stages one row per matching snapshot. A consumer wanting (period, timestep) per row joins the snapshot's properties.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
schema = Schema(
    dimensions={
        "entity": Dimension(dtype=nw.String()),
        "period": Dimension(dtype=nw.Int64()),
        "snapshot": Dimension(dtype=nw.Int64()),
    },
    properties={
        "snapshot": {
            "period": PropertySpec(into="period"),
            "timestep": PropertySpec(dtype=nw.Datetime("us")),
        }
    },
    attributes={
        "p_max_pu": AttributeSpec(dtype=nw.Float64(), dims={"entity", "snapshot"})
    },
)

w.add("period", [2030, 2040])
w.add(
    "snapshot", [0, 1, 2, 3], period=[2030, 2030, 2040, 2040], timestep=[t0, t1, t0, t1]
)
w.set("p_max_pu", 0.8, entity="g1", period=2030)  # snapshots 0 and 1
w.set("p_max_pu", 0.5, entity="g1", timestep=t0)  # snapshots 0 and 2
w.set("snapshot.period", {3: 2030})  # was refused on a nested dim
w.remove("period", [2040])  # refused while a snapshot.period names it
record.dims["snapshot"]  # snapshot
record.properties["snapshot"]  # snapshot | period | timestep

docs.title: Implementation notes
docs.text:
1. Schema: Dimension.within, its validation, _ancestors and axis_key go, callers keying by the dim; a within in a manifest refused naming into; the property-name and versioning rules lose within.
  2. Read: the axis fold, dead labels and dims/properties frames keyed by the label.
  3. Writer: an axis file's columns are the dim and its properties; every into property and group field checked against live labels.
  4. WorkingRecord: add without parent keys, set on any dim's property, remove's cascade and into refusal, the trait check and staging keys over every dim.
  5. Tool: flat snapshot, snapshot.period, snapshot.timestep; series over snapshot alone; build from the properties.
  6. Pages, usage, changelog, tests; DEP 12's and 13's links to the removed within anchors retargeted, which fixes a link and revises no argument.

Checks: no within or axis_key in src/; a multi-period network with repeating timesteps and one with unique ones round-trip; remove("period", …) is refused while a snapshot names it, by remove and by the writer; a manifest declaring within is refused naming into.

docs.title: Rejected Ideas
docs.text:
• A group over (period, timestep) as the snapshot: a masked product, which math-spec's guidance rejects, and a struct-valued key in every time series.
  • Keeping within beside the property: two spellings of one relation, and every special case above stays for the one that keeps it.
  • Composite string labels as a rule ("2030|t1"): the source picks its labels, and a rule would have the record parse them.

docs.title: Open Issues
docs.text:
• Whether Schema should offer a helper that declares a dim with its parent property in one call.
  • Whether the selector needs a qualified form when two reached dims declare period.
  • The NULL-parent pointwise set bug, for schemas with two whole-owned dims.

docs.title: DEP 16: remove traits
docs.text: DEP 16 Title remove traits Author Jonas Hoersch Status Implemented (2026-10-20) Created 2026-10-20 Version Unreleased Replaces DEP 1 (its traits), DEP 3 (switches)

docs.title: Abstract
docs.text: Trait leaves the schema, with its manifest form and every rule reading it. An attribute reaches every label its dims address, and a property every label of its subject. Categories and default_by stay. A tool that needs a per-type vocabulary keeps it itself.

docs.title: Motivation
docs.text:
A trait narrows which labels of a categorized dim carry an attribute or property. That one rule reaches far:

  • The read path. A NULL over a categorized dim expands only to the labels carrying it. categories.carriers builds a (label, attribute) relation per category combination for that.
  • flags(**categories) drops the attributes a category does not carry.
  • set validation refuses a value on a label whose category does not carry the attribute.
  • Compatibility. Schema._dropped_by_category compares every category of two schemas.
  • switch is declared and validated but read by nothing.
  • The schema check. _check_trait holds six rules on on, the bundle and the switch.

One consumer uses it: the PyPSA tool. It derives one trait per component type from PyPSA's registry and asks attributes_for which attributes a type takes. That answer is PyPSA's, read back from a schema the tool wrote. The record layer stores it, folds by it and validates against it, for a vocabulary it never defines.

The "queryable vocabulary" a trait promised (everything investable) has no caller.

docs.title: What goes
docs.text: construct becomes Trait, Schema.traits, traits: in a manifest gone; a manifest declaring traits is refused at load Trait.switch gone; the switch attribute stays an ordinary attribute Schema.attributes_for(dim, **categories) gone; [a for a in schema.attributes if schema.addresses(a, dim)] Schema.properties_for(subject, **categories) gone; schema.properties[subject] narrowed broadcast (categories.carriers) a NULL reaches every label of the dim flags(**categories) filtering by carried attribute rows reaching a matching label decide, nothing else set refusing a label whose category lacks it gone; the label check stays _dropped_by_category in compatibility gone

docs.title: What stays
docs.text:
• Categories. An Enum property of a partial dim still categorizes it. Schema.categorizing, require_categorizing and require_listed stay.
  • default_by keys on a categorizing property, as before. default_for(name, **categories) is unchanged. It never depended on traits.
  • partial is unchanged. It was a condition for a category, not a trait input.
  • Category selection. flags(ctype="Generator") and a property keyword in set select labels by category, as before.
  • with_defaults applies default_for per category combination. Every name is carried, so its _carries_ columns go.

docs.title: The manifest
docs.text:
traits is no field of Schema, and extra="forbid" would refuse it generically. A mode="before" validator refuses it first, as within is refused:

a schema takes no `traits`: an attribute reaches every label its `dims`
address; scope a value with a category keyword on `set`, and keep a
per-type vocabulary in the tool that needs it

docs.title: The PyPSA tool
docs.text:
• _registry_schema declares no traits. It keeps carries, the per-type input names, as a cached _carried(ctype).
  • _NetworkSource.schema adds a type's custom columns to that map, not to a trait.
  • _verify and build ask _carried(ctype) where they asked attributes_for(ENTITY, ctype=ctype).
  • The static frame keeps the entity properties _carried(ctype) names, where it asked carried_properties.

docs.title: Rationale
docs.text:
The narrowing is the tool's knowledge. PyPSA's registry already says which attributes a Load takes. Copying that into the schema makes the record enforce a framework vocabulary. The module layout keeps framework knowledge out of core.

A broadcast over every label is the general rule. Every uncategorized dim already broadcasts that way. A categorized dim was the one exception, and the fold, flags and validation each carried a branch for it.

default_by is not a trait. It picks a value per category, never whether one exists. So it survives unchanged.

Costs. set("p_max_pu", 0.9) now also reaches loads, which PyPSA ignores. A misplaced value is no longer refused on write. A NULL row expands over every label in the owner map, not only carriers. Every record declaring traits is re-exported, breaking changes being free.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
Before:

Schema(
    ...,
    traits={
        "dispatchable": Trait(
            attributes={"p_max_pu"},
            on={"entity.ctype": {"Generator", "StorageUnit"}},
        )
    },
)
w.set("p_max_pu", 0.9)  # every generator and storage unit, never a load
schema.attributes_for("entity", ctype="Load")  # no p_max_pu

After:

Schema(...)  # no traits
w.set("p_max_pu", 0.9, ctype=["Generator", "StorageUnit"])  # one row per label
w.set("p_max_pu", 0.9)  # every entity; a load's value is never read by PyPSA
schema.default_for("p_min_pu", ctype="StorageUnit")  # -1, as before

docs.title: Implementation notes
docs.text:
